content.text:
I drafted a comment-only review of #22, and nothing is posted yet. It answers every open decision addressed to you. The contract is solid, so the review is mostly confirmations plus a few gaps to close.

## Your answers to the open decisions
| Decision | Answer |
|---|---|
| Parallel Generic Netlink ops | **Yes**, on the condition that `RENEW` never waits on `cfg_lock` |
| `EXCHANGE_RX` unicast, `ENOBUFS` means resync | **Confirmed.** I checked the v6.18 source: a full buffer drops the event and flags `ENOBUFS` once per congestion episode |
| Close admission when the owner socket releases | **Confirmed** |
| Owner-epoch/revision binding, re-stage after a new claim | **Confirmed**, with two small gaps to fix |
| PMTU-only change | **Disruptive, for that slot only.** The design requires both ends to agree on `P` in the handshake, and a changed budget is "freshly established" |
| Controller keeps its socket open for the lease | **Yes** |

## What I'm asking Aayush to change
- **Classification must be per slot and complete.** "The whole delta decides" reads as global. It also omits local identity, LAN address, underlay address or interface, role and PMTU. I proposed the full table. I'll implement the same table in the controller for RJ4.
- **Lease-lost and stale-revision can't share `-ESTALE`.** The controller must tell them apart: a lost lease means discard everything and re-claim, while a stale revision only needs a resync.
- **Say who creates `vpn0`.** I suggested provisioning does it before `CLAIM`, and a controller shutdown never deletes it.
- **Smaller points:** the `CONTROLLER_ID` wording, and the controller's renewal timing (`CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, not Rust's default `Instant`).
- **Outside my domain, flagged with a hedge:** §3 reads the lease epoch and deadline as two separate words. A claim racing between the two loads could briefly admit an old-epoch peer, and ARM64/Pi 5 can reorder those loads.

## A gap in my own code
My #15 transport silently drops any message whose sequence number doesn't match the outstanding request. `EXCHANGE_RX` events arrive on the owner's socket, so they would be lost while a reply is awaited. The review says so and commits me to a bounded event queue in the command-client PR.

## The review text I'd post
> ABI/controller-domain review of revision 2 (`14b44cf`). Comment only; this is not an approval. I read the whole contract against TECHNICAL_DESIGN §§8, 9, 13, 14 and 17, #12, the Netlink transport I merged in #15 and the config rules in #17. The Linux facts below are checked against the v6.18 source.
>
> **Answers to the DECIDE items**
> 1. **Parallel ops: yes.** Renewals are once per second with 5 s validity, and up to eight gateways can share a test host, so one gateway's slow request must not wait behind a global mutex. Condition: `RENEW` takes only `lease_lock` plus an RCU read of the current revision, never `cfg_lock`. Please say so in §3 and add a §8 case where renewals keep succeeding while a maximal `VALIDATE`/`COMMIT` of the same gateway is stalled.
> 2. **`EXCHANGE_RX` unicast, `ENOBUFS` = resync: confirmed.** In v6.18, `genlmsg_unicast()` → `netlink_unicast(MSG_DONTWAIT)`; on a full buffer `netlink_attachskb()` calls `netlink_overrun()`, which drops the event and sets `ENOBUFS` on the receiver unless `NETLINK_NO_ENOBUFS` is set, once per congestion episode. So the contract should require the drop counter in `STATUS`/`COUNTERS`. The controller will not set `NETLINK_NO_ENOBUFS`, will treat `ENOBUFS` as "re-read `STATUS`, rely on INIT/RESPONSE retries", and will never close and reopen its socket to recover.
> 3. **Close admission on owner release: confirmed.** The controller uses `SOCK_CLOEXEC` and spawns no children that inherit the socket. A restarted controller can re-`CLAIM` right after the old socket closes; a hung one must wait for expiry, so `-EBUSY` on `CLAIM` means "retry with backoff for up to 5 s".
> 4. **Owner-epoch/revision binding and recovery: confirmed.** After any new claim the controller re-stages from scratch (`CLAIM`, `VALIDATE`, `COMMIT_CONFIG`, then fresh establishment), with the route/perimeter transaction around the commit (HR1 §3). Gaps: define the revision after owner loss unpublishes the config (I suggest it resets to 0), and have the `CLAIM` reply return the current revision.
> 5. **PMTU-only change: disruptive, for that slot only.** Both endpoints must configure the same `P` and validate it during establishment (§15); `P` is in the handshake payload (bytes 92-95), bound into the transcript, and a changed budget is "freshly established". Other peers stay eligible; only the shared `vpn0` transmit MTU is recomputed.
> 6. **Controller keeps its socket open for the whole lease: yes.** The same socket must claim, send every owner-gated request and receive `EXCHANGE_RX`.
>
> **Requests before this becomes the shared contract**
> - **A. Make classification per slot and complete (§4).** "The whole delta decides" reads as global, but §13 and the independent-peer cases need unrelated peers to stay eligible. Also cover: local identity, LAN address/prefix, underlay address/interface, a slot's role and PMTU. All disruptive; local ones affect every peer, per-slot ones only that slot. Only ACL rule changes are policy-only. I will implement this exact table in RJ4; each row needs an acceptance case.
> - **B. Distinguish "lease lost" from "stale revision".** §3 uses `-ESTALE` for a late renewal and #28 uses it for stale revision/incarnation too. Recovery differs, so give lease-expired its own errno or stable reason.
> - **C. Say who creates `vpn0`.** I suggest provisioning, idempotently, before `CLAIM`; a controller shutdown never deletes it (HR1 §3).
> - **D. `CONTROLLER_ID` wording.** "Fresh per `CLAIM`" conflicts with "same ID behaves as `RENEW`". Say the ID is chosen per ownership attempt and reused only for renewals.
> - **E. Timing.** The controller will use `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` for renewals (Rust's `Instant` is `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`) and keep request timeouts below the 1 s renewal period.
>
> **Outside my domain, flagging.** §3 admits with two independent `READ_ONCE` words. A reader can load the old `live_epoch`, a `CLAIM`-after-expiry on another CPU can then store the new epoch and deadline, and the reader sees (old epoch, new deadline) and admits a stale peer. Tiny window, but formally an admission at/after expiry, and ARM64 can reorder. State the load/store order with acquire/release, or mark old peers ineligible under their locks before publishing. I may be missing a rule that covers this.
>
> **Controller-side commitments.** One socket per gateway in the gateway's namespace; one request in flight; a bounded event queue so `EXCHANGE_RX` is never discarded while awaiting a reply (my #15 transport currently drops non-matching sequence numbers, a gap in my code); `ENOBUFS` resync; and a test client for the §8 control-message cases.

Two honesty notes: I haven't run anything against Aayush's kernel for #22 (it's a document-only PR), and the `ENOBUFS` behavior is from reading the v6.18 source, not from a test against his module.

Tell me whether to post it as written or what to change.

## Behavior and scope

Work package AY3 (owner: Aayush), one component. Adds `struct vpt1_generation` (`kernel/crypto/generation.c`, `kernel/include/vpt1_generation.h`): a directional key pair with separate immutable TX and RX AEAD transforms, built on the merged counter/replay helpers. It enforces the design's age and usage limits, rejects equal TX/RX keys, and frees (and erases) its keys in process context after the last reference, even when that put happens in softirq. `vpt1_sequence` gains two read-only usage accessors (`vpt1_tx_usage`/`vpt1_rx_usage`).

**This is not wired into the foundation module and does no packet parsing, skb handling or output.** The peer state machine (AY4), crypto-request ownership/async completion and runtime accounting (AY5) are separate. Details and limits: [docs/AY3_GENERATION.md](docs/AY3_GENERATION.md).

Design: TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md sections 4.3, 7 and 14; contract with `docs/AY1_OWNERSHIP.md` (key generation owned by the peer, requests hold references, erase after disabled references drain).

## Contracts and correctness

- No wire, Netlink ABI, limit or lock-order change. Lock order is unchanged: generation code takes only the existing sequence locks.
- New API surface is documented in the header. `now_ns` is a parameter so tests inject a clock; production passes boot time.
- `vpt1_generation_exit()` must follow release of every generation; a put after exit WARNs and leaks rather than freeing in softirq.

## Validation evidence

On the `6.18.0-vpt1-ref` x86-64 guest (4096-byte pages, QEMU/WHPX; a long-lived working copy of the reference image, not a fresh overlay): `make -C kernel W=1` has no warnings; `insmod` reports `VPT1_GENERATION_TEST: assertions=68 failures=0 PASS`; module unloads; no BUG/WARNING/Oops/refcount/UBSAN/KASAN markers.

Mutation checks (each fails the test; the unmutated source passes again): drop the equal-key check (2 failures), `>` instead of `>=` for the hard age (6), RX accessor returns the TX transform (5).

**NOT_RUN:** ARM64/Pi 5 16 KiB pages, Clang, KASAN/KCSAN/lockdep (the guest kernel has `CONFIG_DEBUG_ATOMIC_SLEEP` off, so the softirq-put test cannot detect a sleep in atomic context), allocation-failure paths, and any CI lane (main has none for kernel code).

## Review

- [ ] @HarshDhru23: lifetime and deferred-free design, and that his HR2/witness code only borrows a generation through a peer reference
- [ ] @rajmodi8905: key orientation (initiator TX = k1, responder RX = k1) as seen by the controller's Split handoff
- [ ] @AnvitAggarwal: reproduction, and where the leak counter belongs in the AY5 harness

----- discussion

##### docs
# AY3 directional key generation

Owner: Aayush. Reviewers: Harsh (kernel lifetime), Raj (key orientation). This is a
component of AY3, not a working VPN: nothing links it into the foundation module yet,
and it does no packet parsing, skb handling or output.

`kernel/crypto/generation.c` adds `struct vpt1_generation`, one directional key pair
(TECHNICAL_DESIGN sections 4.3, 7 and 14) built on the merged counter/replay helpers in
`vpt1_sequence.h`.

## Contract

| Rule | How it is enforced |
|---|---|
| Separate immutable TX and RX keys | Two `rfc7539(chacha20,poly1305)` transforms, keyed once in `create`; there is no way to rekey in place. |
| Distinct keys per direction | `create` rejects equal keys (`-EINVAL`): one key in both directions would reuse (key, nonce) at counter zero. |
| Single reservation owner | TX counters come only from `vpt1_generation_tx_reserve()` (wraps `vpt1_tx_reserve()`); never refunded. |
| Replay claimed after authentication | `rx_precheck` is read-only; `rx_accept` rechecks and claims under the sequence lock, only after AEAD success. |
| Hard age 180 s, soft 120 s | `now_ns` is passed in (boot time in production, synthetic in tests). A hard-aged generation disables itself and returns `-EKEYEXPIRED`. |
| Soft and hard record/byte limits | `vpt1_generation_limit()` reports the worst of age, records and bytes over both directions. |
| Keys erased after the last reference | The final `put` disables the generation and queues the free, so it is safe from softirq; the work frees both transforms and `kfree_sensitive()`s the object. |
| Leak accounting | `vpt1_generation_live()` counts allocated minus freed; AY5 can export it from debug builds. |

The state machine (pending/current/retiring), rekey grants and activation are AY4's and
stay with the peer, not here.

## Tests

`tests/unit/vpt1_generation_test.c` (standalone adapter, and KUnit when enabled), 68
assertions in four groups:

- initiator/responder orientation: A's TX output opens only with B's RX transform, not
  with A's own RX transform, not with a wrong counter; both directions; replay (`-EALREADY`)
  after a successful open; equal keys refused;
- age limits at exactly 120 s and 180 s (and one nanosecond before), disabled afterwards,
  and the same for RX;
- 524,288/1,048,576 records and the 512 MiB soft byte limit with maximum-size records;
- references and deferred free, including a final put under `local_bh_disable()`.

## Evidence (3 November 2026, build and test host: `6.18.0-vpt1-ref`, x86-64, 4096-byte pages)

`make -C kernel W=1` builds with no warnings. `insmod` reports
`VPT1_GENERATION_TEST: assertions=68 failures=0 PASS`, the module unloads, and dmesg has
no BUG/WARNING/Oops/refcount/UBSAN/KASAN markers. Three deliberate mutations each made the
test fail and the unmutated source passes again: dropping the equal-key check (2 failures),
`>` instead of `>=` for the hard age (6), and returning the TX transform for RX (5).

The guest was a long-lived working copy of the reference image, not a fresh overlay.

## Not covered

- ARM64 and Pi 5 (16 KiB pages); Clang; KASAN, KCSAN and lockdep. The guest kernel has
  `CONFIG_DEBUG_ATOMIC_SLEEP` off, so the softirq-put test checks behavior only and cannot
  detect a sleep in atomic context.
- A production `seal`/`open` API over skbs and scatterlists, crypto-request ownership and
  asynchronous completion (AY5), and the peer state machine (AY4).
- Allocation-failure paths of `create`.

index 22d8d91..c77529d 100644
--- a/kernel/crypto/sequence.c
+++ b/kernel/crypto/sequence.c
@@ -133,3 +133,19 @@ void vpt1_rx_disable(struct vpt1_rx_sequence *state)
 	state->disabled = true;
 	spin_unlock_bh(&state->lock);
 }
+

+{

+	*records = atomic64_read(&state->next);

+	spin_unlock_bh(&state->lock);
+}
+
+void vpt1_rx_usage(struct vpt1_rx_sequence *state, u64 *records, u64 *bytes)
+{

+	*records = state->records;
+	*bytes = state->bytes;

+}

index 767f761..5474304 100644
--- a/kernel/include/vpt1_sequence.h
+++ b/kernel/include/vpt1_sequence.h
@@ -58,4 +58,8 @@ int vpt1_rx_accept_authenticated(struct vpt1_rx_sequence *state, u64 counter,
 				 u32 plaintext_len);
 void vpt1_rx_disable(struct vpt1_rx_sequence *state);
 
+/* Consistent snapshot of the charged usage under the state's lock. */
+void vpt1_tx_usage(struct vpt1_tx_sequence *state, u64 *records, u64 *bytes);
+void vpt1_rx_usage(struct vpt1_rx_sequence *state, u64 *records, u64 *bytes);
+
 #endif /* VPT1_SEQUENCE_H */
##### design limits table
The receive replay window is **1024 counters** per direction/generation. Bit zero represents the highest accepted counter. Packets ahead of the window may shift it only after successful authentication; authenticated but already accepted counters and counters more than 1023 behind the highest are dropped. Initial state has no accepted counter, not an implicitly accepted zero.

Two concurrent decryptions can pass a cheap preliminary check, but acceptance performs a second test and bitmap update under the same per-generation replay lock. Only one can claim a counter. Authentication failure never updates this bitmap. After successful authentication, a structurally invalid or ineligible record consumes its counter and is dropped rather than being processed repeatedly.

Key age is measured using suspend-inclusive monotonic boot time. The earlier of the following limits applies independently to TX and RX, counting **all** protected control/data records:

| Quantity | Soft limit | Hard limit |
|---|---|---|
| Age from candidate key installation | 120 seconds | 180 seconds |
| Records per direction | 524,288 | 1,048,576 |
| Authenticated plaintext bytes per direction, including the 4-byte record prefix | 512 MiB | 1 GiB |

TX reserves record/byte allowance before encrypting. Gaps and failed outputs do not refund counters. RX commits accepted-record/byte charges with replay acceptance. A record that would exceed a hard bound is not delivered. These deliberately conservative project limits are operational choices, not calculated guarantees of immunity to every cryptographic attack. Tag failures are rate-limited and counted but do not independently revoke trusted state.

Sleep/resume, snapshot restoration, and cloning of live state do not preserve active eligibility. Supported environments must prevent these transitions while active or invalidate keys/flows before forwarding resumes, using fresh randomness for recovery. A wall-clock change alone does not reset a key age or counter.

Key-orientation review for the controller's Split handoff. Comment only; this is not an approval. I did not review the deferred-free lifetime design (Harsh's domain).

**Orientation as designed.** TECHNICAL_DESIGN §3.1: the initiator installs TX=k1, RX=k2 and the responder TX=k2, RX=k1. `vpt1_generation_create(tx_key, rx_key, now)` takes already-oriented keys and does no swapping: `tx_key` keys `tx_aead`, `rx_key` keys `rx_aead`. The controller's `SessionKeys` is already oriented that way, and in #28 `op_stage()` passes `TX_KEY` to `tx` and `RX_KEY` to `rx` in order. So the mapping is a straight copy end to end, as long as the controller never swaps.

**Checked against real controller output, not assumed.** On the AN1 reference VM (`6.18.0-vpt1-ref`, x86-64, 4096-byte pages, booted under QEMU TCG on a Mac), I patched a scratch copy of `vpt1_generation_test.c` so the two ends of the orientation test are built from the keys my controller's real handshake produced (`Initiator::finish` for the initiator, `respond` for the responder), with no assumption about which is k1 or k2:

- three independent handshakes: `VPT1_GENERATION_TEST: assertions=68 failures=0 PASS` each time, `make -C kernel W=1` with no warnings;
- deliberately swapping the initiator's TX and RX keys: `failures=4 FAIL` (lines 156, 167, 168 of the round-trip test) and `insmod` returns `EINVAL`;
- restoring the real keys: PASS again.

So the controller's TX/RX pairing and the kernel generation object agree: the initiator's TX output opens only with the responder's RX transform, not with the initiator's own RX transform. The checked-in test is unchanged by this; it was a scratch run.

**Suggestion (non-blocking).** The checked-in test only uses fixed seed keys. Once #13 merges, please add its public vector keys (`initiator_tx` `71a19894...0b56`, `initiator_rx` `f3405d87...f81d`, mirrored for the responder) as one fixture in this orientation test. That gives a standing cross-component regression, so a future change to either side's Split handling fails in CI instead of in an end-to-end run.

**Controller side.** The key buffers I send are `Zeroizing` on my side, and I see `op_stage()` wipes the request's copy in the kernel with `memzero_explicit` whatever the result, which is the behavior §3.1 wants.

Not covered by this review: ARM64/Pi 5, Clang, KASAN/KCSAN/lockdep, and the allocation-failure paths of `create`.
EOF

The #26 review is drafted and key orientation checks out. Yes, we can open new PRs now. Nothing is posted yet.

## The #26 review (key orientation)
The controller's keys and the kernel's key object agree. I tested this with real handshakes, not by reading the code:
- **Design check:** the design says the initiator sends with k1 and the responder with k2. The kernel's `create(tx_key, rx_key)` takes keys already oriented and never swaps them. Aayush's draft #28 passes `TX_KEY` and `RX_KEY` through in order.
- **Real-key test (reference VM, x86-64):** I patched a scratch copy of his orientation test so its two ends use keys from my controller's handshakes, with no assumption about which is k1 or k2.
  - Three independent handshakes each gave 68/68 pass, with no build warnings.
  - Deliberately swapping the initiator's keys failed 4 assertions and the module refused to load.
  - Restoring the real keys passed again.
- **Suggestion (non-blocking):** once #13 merges, add its public vector keys as a permanent fixture in his test. That would make a future Split-handling change fail in CI rather than in an end-to-end run.
- **Not reviewed:** the deferred-free lifetime design (Harsh's area), ARM64/Pi 5, Clang, KASAN and lockdep.

## Can we open new PRs? Yes, with one blocker
#17 and #29 are merged. #29 was Aayush covering Anvit's manifest request, so that follow-up is already done. #12 (Netlink IDs) is still an open draft, so those IDs aren't on main yet.

| PR idea | Status |
|---|---|
| **Transport event queue and `ENOBUFS` handling** (small): stop dropping unsolicited kernel messages. I committed to this in the #22 review. | Unblocked |
| **Handshake attempt manager** (RJ2/RJ5): 10 s attempt deadline, 20 s response cache, conflicting-INIT and rate-limit policy, key-erasure audit. | Unblocked |
| **Config-change classification** (RJ4): which changes are disruptive per slot, following the table in my #22 review. | Unblocked, but may need small edits if Aayush's contract revision differs |
| **`vptunnel` command client** | **Blocked** until #12 merges and the per-command table is agreed |

## Still pending for you
- Reviews on #24, #25, #23 and #27, plus re-checks of #18 and #21.
- Aayush hasn't yet replied to the #22 review.

Tell me whether to post the #26 review and start the event-queue PR first.

The controller's `SessionKeys` is already oriented that way, and in #28 `op_stage()` passes `TX_KEY` to `tx` and `RX_KEY` to `rx` in order.
>
> **Checked against real controller output, not assumed.** On the AN1 reference VM (`6.18.0-vpt1-ref`, x86-64, 4096-byte pages, booted under QEMU TCG on a Mac), I patched a scratch copy of `vpt1_generation_test.c` so the two ends of the orientation test are built from the keys my controller's real handshake produced, with no assumption about which is k1 or k2:
> - three independent handshakes: `VPT1_GENERATION_TEST: assertions=68 failures=0 PASS` each time, `make -C kernel W=1` with no warnings;
> - deliberately swapping the initiator's TX and RX keys: `failures=4 FAIL` (lines 156, 167, 168 of the round-trip test) and `insmod` returns `EINVAL`;
> - restoring the real keys: PASS again.
>
> So the controller's TX/RX pairing and the kernel generation object agree: the initiator's TX output opens only with the responder's RX transform, not with the initiator's own RX transform. The checked-in test is unchanged by this; it was a scratch run.
>
> **Suggestion (non-blocking).** The checked-in test only uses fixed seed keys. Once #13 merges, please add its public vector keys (`initiator_tx` `71a19894...0b56`, `initiator_rx` `f3405d87...f81d`, mirrored for the responder) as one fixture in this orientation test. That gives a standing cross-component regression.
>
> **Controller side.** The key buffers I send are `Zeroizing` on my side, and I see `op_stage()` wipes the request's copy in the kernel with `memzero_explicit` whatever the result, which is the behavior §3.1 wants.
>
> Not covered by this review: ARM64/Pi 5, Clang, KASAN/KCSAN/lockdep, and the allocation-failure paths of `create`.

## Generic Netlink transport (`src/genl/`)

Family-independent layer under the `vptunnel` client (TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md
section 17). Netlink integers are host-endian with 4-byte alignment, unlike
the big-endian VPT1 wire format.

- `message` (portable): request builder with typed attributes, zero padding,
  rejection of type 0/flag bits and of anything over 64 KiB; the buffer is
  `Zeroizing` because STAGE_GENERATION will carry raw keys. Strict splitting of
  received datagrams, ACK/error classification (positive or `i32::MIN` codes
  rejected), generic attribute walking, and `nlctrl` family lookup with
  duplicate/missing/mismatched-name checks.
- `inbox` (portable): the whole receive path behind a small `Source` trait, so
  every branch is tested without a kernel. The owner socket carries replies
  **and** kernel events (`EXCHANGE_RX` is a unicast to the owner's port, and
  ownership is bound to that port, so both must share one socket). By
  `nlmsg_seq`: `0` with a family message type is an *event* and is queued
  (at most 64 events / 256 KiB; the newest are dropped and counted when full);
  the awaited sequence is the reply; any other nonzero sequence is a stale
  reply to an abandoned request, dropped and counted. A whole datagram is
  always consumed, so an event sharing one with the ACK is kept. One total
  deadline covers a request however many events arrive, so a flood cannot
  stretch a lease renewal. Datagrams not sent by the kernel (port 0) are never
  trusted. A kernel `ENOBUFS` or a queue overflow sets a flag read once with
  `take_events_lost()`: the controller then resyncs from `STATUS`. It must
  never close and reopen the socket to recover, because releasing it releases
  the lease.
- `socket` (Linux only): one bound `NETLINK_GENERIC` socket via `rustix`, so the
  crate stays `forbid(unsafe_code)`; it is only the OS read behind `inbox`.
  Requests use nonzero sequence numbers, always ask for an ACK, and the
  request budget is a total (`open(request_budget)`), not per read. Multipart
  dumps are refused. `recv_event(timeout)` returns the next event.

AY2 requirement this relies on: kernel events must use `nlmsg_seq` 0
(`EXCHANGE_RX`, command 128). A nonzero sequence would be dropped as a stale
reply.

`tests/genl_linux.rs` runs against the real kernel's built-in `nlctrl` family,
so it needs neither the module nor root: name and id lookup, ENOENT/EINVAL
error paths, socket reuse after errors, idle `recv_event`, clean counters after

cd "/Users/rajmodi/Documents/5th sem/CN/VPNTunnel/.claude/worktrees/testing-strategy-linux-12bffd" && gh pr create --repo Aayush75/VPNTunnel --base main --head codex/raj/genl-events --title "RJ3: keep kernel events on the owner socket and bound the receive path" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Behavior and scope

Work package **RJ3** (owner: Raj). Design: TECHNICAL_DESIGN §17 and `docs/AY2_CONTRACT.md` §2/§3 (#22). This fixes a gap in my merged transport (#15) that I flagged in my #22 review.

**The problem.** The owner socket carries replies *and* unsolicited kernel events: `EXCHANGE_RX` is a unicast to the owner's port, and ownership is bound to that port (`RENEW` needs the exact owner triple), so requests and events must share one socket. #15's `transact()` discarded every message whose sequence number did not match the outstanding request, so an event arriving while a reply was awaited was lost. Its timeout was also per read, so a stream of events could stretch one request to many timeouts, which matters when a lease is 5 s and renewals are 1 s apart.

**The change.**
- **`control/src/genl/inbox.rs` (portable, new).** The receive path moves behind a small `Source` trait, so every branch is testable without a kernel. By `nlmsg_seq`: `0` with a family message type is an **event**, queued (at most 64 events / 256 KiB; the newest are dropped and counted when full); the awaited sequence is the **reply**; any other nonzero sequence is a **stale reply** to an abandoned request, dropped and counted (this controller's sequence numbers start at 1). A whole datagram is always consumed, so an event sharing one with the ACK is kept, and the first terminal result for the awaited sequence wins.
- **One total deadline per request** (`open(request_budget)` is now a total, not per read), so a flood cannot extend a renewal.
- **Lost events are reported, not hidden.** A kernel `ENOBUFS` or a local queue overflow sets a flag read once through `take_events_lost()`. The controller then resyncs from `STATUS`. It must never close and reopen the socket to recover, because releasing the socket releases the lease (docs say so).
- **Non-kernel senders are never trusted** (port != 0), so a forged event or ACK from another socket is ignored.
- **`control/src/genl/socket.rs`** shrinks to the OS read (`Wire`) plus `GenlSocket::{recv_event, take_events_lost, pending_events, stats}`. `TransportError` and `OwnedReply` moved into `inbox` and are re-exported from `socket`, so existing paths still work.

## Contracts and correctness

- **No ABI, wire or kernel change.** One assumption on the kernel side: events use `nlmsg_seq` 0. I checked #28: `vpt1_netlink_exchange_rx()` calls `genlmsg_put(skb, 0, 0, ...)` (portid 0, seq 0) and `genlmsg_unicast()`, which matches. The README records this as a requirement on AY2, since a nonzero sequence would be dropped as a stale reply. Events are deliberately not required to carry this socket's port in `nlmsg_pid`, since that kernel call sets 0.
- **Behavior change:** `GenlSocket::open`'s argument is now the total per-request budget. The only in-tree callers are the #15 tests.
- Kernel `ENOBUFS` semantics are from the v6.18 source (`genlmsg_unicast()` calls `netlink_unicast(MSG_DONTWAIT)`; `netlink_attachskb()` then calls `netlink_overrun()`, which sets `ENOBUFS` once per congestion episode), not from a live test.

## Validation evidence

Commit `e4bb8ea`, running `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`:

| Environment | Result |
|---|---|
| **AN1 reference VM** `6.18.0-vpt1-ref` x86-64 (booted on an Apple Silicon Mac under QEMU TCG) | Clean; **100 pass** unprivileged (68 library, 11 real-kernel, 21 others) **plus the 2 privileged `#[ignore]`d forgery tests as root** |
| macOS 27.0.1, Apple M4 | Clean; 89 portable tests pass (the Linux socket tests compile out) |

The source tree (everything except the README) hashed identically on both machines.

**New tests.** 23 portable tests in `genl::inbox`: event before, after and inside the ACK's datagram; ordering; stale replies; kernel error with events preserved; first-terminal-wins; flood bounded by count and by bytes (with the lost flag and the byte budget freed on drain); `ENOBUFS`; timeout; interrupted reads; forged non-kernel datagrams; wrong-port reply; sequence-0 control messages; multipart, too-many-replies, DONE and malformed datagrams; the total deadline under an endless slow flood (it holds); `run_events` ordering, early wake on `ENOBUFS` and idle timeout. Real-kernel: idle `recv_event`, clean counters after 40 mixed requests, and two root-only tests that forge a kernel-looking event and a matching ACK from a second socket.

**Mutations (each caught):**
- discarding events (the old behavior) fails 12 tests;
- trusting non-kernel senders fails 2 portable tests **and both real-kernel forgery tests**;
- silent queue overflow fails 2;
- ignoring `ENOBUFS` fails 1;
- stopping at the ACK mid-datagram fails 2.

Code was restored and verified byte-identical after each.

Two mistakes in my own first draft of the tests, fixed before this commit: I expected padding bytes in a payload (the length field excludes padding) and a full queue of 64 under a 150 ms flood that only reads about 25 events.

**Not run:** real kernel `ENOBUFS` delivery (needs a kernel event producer, so the `vptunnel` module from #28); the forgery tests in CI (they need `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, so they are `#[ignore]`d and visible as ignored); ARM64/Pi 5.

## Review and remaining work

- **Reviewers:** Aayush (the seq-0 requirement on `EXCHANGE_RX`, `ENOBUFS` handling and the owner-socket contract) and Anvit (test lanes; whether the root-only forgery tests belong in a privileged CI job).
- **Next RJ3 steps:** the `vptunnel` command client on this transport, once #12 and the per-command table are agreed; then the lease/renewal loop and key handoff.
EOF

content.text:
I posted the #26 review and opened [PR #31](https://github.com/Aayush75/VPNTunnel/pull/31), the transport event-queue fix. All six CI checks pass, including the new `netns-smoke` and `ci-gate` jobs that main now has, and nothing is left uncommitted.

## #26 review (posted)
- Posted as a [comment-only review](https://github.com/Aayush75/VPNTunnel/pull/26#pullrequestreview-5748359775).
- It reports that the controller's real handshake keys, fed into Aayush's kernel key object, open records only in the opposite direction. A deliberately swapped version fails.

## PR #31: stop losing kernel events
- **The bug (mine, from #15):** the socket threw away any message that didn't match the request being waited on. But the kernel sends `EXCHANGE_RX` events to the owner's socket, and ownership is bound to that same socket. So events arriving mid-request were lost. The timeout was also per read, so an event flood could stretch one request far past a 5 s lease's renewal budget.
- **What it does:**
  - Messages with sequence 0 are kept as events, in a bounded queue of 64.
  - Replies to abandoned requests are dropped and counted.
  - One total deadline covers each request, however many events arrive.
  - Messages not sent by the kernel are ignored.
  - A kernel `ENOBUFS`, or a full queue, sets a flag. When it's set, the controller re-reads `STATUS` instead of assuming it saw every event. It must never close and reopen the socket to recover, because that would release the lease.
- **Matches Aayush's draft:** I checked #28. His `EXCHANGE_RX` code already sends events with sequence 0, so no change is needed on his side.

## How it's tested
- **Reference VM:** 100 tests pass, plus 2 root-only tests that forge a kernel-looking event and a matching ACK from a second socket. The real kernel ignores both.
- **Mac:** 89 portable tests pass.
- **Mutation checks:** I broke each safety property and the tests failed. For example, removing the sender check fails both real-kernel forgery tests.
- **Mistakes in my first test draft, fixed before committing:** one test expected padding bytes in a payload, and one assumed a full queue of 64 under a flood that only reads about 25 events.
- **Not covered:** real kernel `ENOBUFS` delivery, because nothing on the kernel side produces events yet. The forgery tests also aren't in CI, because they need root; they show as "ignored" rather than passing silently.

## Where things stand
- **Reviews you still owe:** #24, #25, #23, #27, plus re-checks of #18 and #21.
- **Still blocked:** the `vptunnel` command client, until #12 merges and the per-command table is agreed.
- **Waiting on Aayush:** a reply to the #22 review.

I'd suggest the #24 and #25 reviews next, since they're assigned to you, then the handshake attempt manager.

content.content:
# The two-Pi demo

Two Raspberry Pis are joined by an Ethernet cable (the underlay). Each Pi hosts a Wi-Fi network with one
laptop on it. **Without the VPN, laptop A cannot reach laptop B. With the VPN running on both Pis, it can,
and each laptop sees the other by its own address, as if they shared a network.**

```
laptop A ~~wifi~~ Pi A (wlan0 10.77.1.1/24) ==== cable ==== Pi B (wlan0 10.77.2.1/24) ~~wifi~~ laptop B
                       eth0 172.31.250.11              eth0 172.31.250.12
```

## What "like the same LAN" means

The tunnel is **routed IPv4**, not a bridge. The two Wi-Fi networks are different subnets (10.77.1.0/24 and
10.77.2.0/24). Anything that works by IP address works across them: ping, web pages, SSH, file sharing by
address, UDP. These do **not** cross: broadcast discovery (mDNS/Bonjour, the "network neighbourhood" list),
and hostnames unless a DNS or hosts entry exists. The laptops are not in one subnet.

## Switching the VPN on and off

On each Pi, as root, with the Pi's own configuration (`demo-pi-a.toml` or `demo-pi-b.toml`, in
`infra/gateway/`, after generating real keys as the file's header says):

```sh
VPTCTL=/usr/local/bin/vptctl VPT1_MODULE=/path/to/vpt1_foundation.ko \
    infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh up   infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml --wait 20   # start B first
infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh status infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh down   infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
```

`up` loads the module if needed, creates `vpn0`, adds the routes to the other Pi's network, installs the
forwarding firewall and the TCP MSS clamp (`mss-clamp.nft`), and starts `vptctl run`. `down` stops the
controller first, which closes the tunnel at once, then removes `vpn0`, the routes and the clamp, and leaves a
firewall that forwards nothing. Everything about the network comes from the one configuration file through
`vptctl perimeter`.

The policy in the demo configurations is whole-network, in both directions on both Pis: ICMP echo, all TCP
ports and all UDP ports between 10.77.1.0/24 and 10.77.2.0/24, so any address the Pi's DHCP server hands out is
covered. Everything else is denied by the kernel's default-deny ACL. The very large UDP datagram limit still
applies (fragments are dropped; see `AY2_DATAPATH.md`, "Packet size").

## Hosting the laptops' Wi-Fi (untested)

`infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh up|down|render CONFIG` runs hostapd and dnsmasq on the configuration's LAN interface, with
the interface, address and network taken from the same file. DHCP hands out .50 to .200 of the /24 with the Pi as the
default gateway and no DNS. It is separate from `vpt-gateway.sh`, so the network can be up with the VPN off, which is
the "laptops cannot see each other" half of the demo. Needs `hostapd` and `dnsmasq` installed:

```sh
VPT_AP_SSID=demo-a VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE='choose-one' VPT_AP_COUNTRY=IN     infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh up infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
```

The passphrase is read from the environment, written only to a `0600` file under `/run/vpt-ap`, and never printed.

## Evidence

`tests/netns/demo_reachability.py` runs the demo with nothing but `vpt-gateway.sh` and the demo
configurations, on the reference VM (x86-64, 6.18, a long-lived working copy of the image, not the AN1 master).
31 checks:

- Before anything starts, laptop A cannot ping or open a connection to laptop B.
- With both Pis up: both directions work for ping, TCP (the server sees the laptop's own source address) and UDP; the
  second laptop on each side, and a second DHCP-style address on a laptop, work too, as source and as destination.
- With the VPN up, a laptop still cannot reach the cable addresses or an address outside the policy.
- Stopping one Pi closes the tunnel in both directions within a few seconds.
- With both Pis down, a laptop still cannot reach the cable even if the other Pi has a route back (checked by
  giving it one), `vpn0` is gone, and switching the VPN on again restores reachability.

A mutation that removes the "off" firewall makes 2 of these fail. The module unloads with no leaked objects.

## Not covered

- **Wi-Fi hosting and DHCP are written but untested.** `infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh` (below) has never been run on a
  Pi. Only its `render` output is tested (`tests/unit/test_ap_script.py`). No second adapter is needed when each Pi's
  only job is this demo: its built-in radio hosts the network and the Ethernet port carries the cable. The radio
  advertises access-point mode (`PLATFORM_PI5.md`), but it has never been tested as one here, so test that early.
  Install packages and set up the Pi while it still has internet; during the demo reach it by joining its own
  Wi-Fi and using SSH to its address (10.77.1.1 or 10.77.2.1).
- **ARM64 and the Pi:** nothing here has run on a Pi. The module has not been built for 6.18 ARM64 with 16 KiB pages.
- **Firewall:** the full HR1 perimeter (`tools/hr1_perimeter.py`) cannot carry traffic yet, because it requires
  packet marks the kernel does not mint (`HR1.md`). `vpt-gateway.sh` installs a smaller forwarding firewall
  (LAN to `vpn0` for the peers' prefixes, nothing else) and the kernel ACL is the actual authorization. Switch to the
  HR1 perimeter once its hooks land.
- No hitless re-keying: about every 90 seconds a few packets are lost during the key change (`CONTROLLER.md`).
- No systemd unit: `up` starts the controller in the background and `down` stops it.
=========== demo-pi-a.toml
# Raspberry Pi gateway A for the two-Pi demo: every laptop on this Pi's Wi-Fi network can reach every
# laptop on the other Pi's network while the VPN is on, and none can when it is off.
#
# The public keys below are the sample values from control/examples; generate real ones on each Pi:
#   vptctl genkey --out /etc/vpntunnel/gw-a.key     (prints the public key to hand to the other Pi)
# and replace the peer's `public_key`. `lan_interface` is the Wi-Fi access-point interface and
# `underlay_interface` the Ethernet port with the cable to the other Pi.
#
# Start and stop with: infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh up|down THIS_FILE
[gateway]
name = "pi-a"
private_key_file = "/etc/vpntunnel/gw-a.key"
lan_interface = "wlan0"
lan_address = "10.77.1.1/24"
underlay_interface = "eth0"
underlay_address = "172.31.250.11/24"

[[peer]]
name = "pi-b"
slot = 1
public_key = "ad8cbe47dec1eb6f5491880eb2612ef18d42b3c667c7b165c4047437fb86861f"
endpoint = "172.31.250.12"
role = "initiator"
path_mtu = 1500
prefixes = ["10.77.2.0/24"]

# Policy: whole-network rules, so any laptop address the Pi's DHCP hands out is covered.
# Both directions are listed on both Pis; every other flow stays denied.

[[rule]]
id = 1
peer = "pi-b"
source = "10.77.1.0/24"
destination = "10.77.2.0/24"
protocol = "icmp-echo"

[[rule]]
id = 2
peer = "pi-b"
source = "10.77.2.0/24"
destination = "10.77.1.0/24"
protocol = "icmp-echo"

[[rule]]
id = 3
peer = "pi-b"
source = "10.77.1.0/24"
destination = "10.77.2.0/24"
protocol = "tcp"
ports = "1-65535"

[[rule]]
id = 4
peer = "pi-b"
source = "10.77.2.0/24"
destination = "10.77.1.0/24"
protocol = "tcp"
ports = "1-65535"

[[rule]]
id = 5
peer = "pi-b"
source = "10.77.1.0/24"
destination = "10.77.2.0/24"
protocol = "udp"
ports = "1-65535"

[[rule]]
id = 6
peer = "pi-b"
source = "10.77.2.0/24"
destination = "10.77.1.0/24"

# The two-Pi demo

Two Raspberry Pis are joined by an Ethernet cable (the underlay). Each Pi hosts a Wi-Fi network with one
laptop on it. **Without the VPN, laptop A cannot reach laptop B. With the VPN running on both Pis, it can,
and each laptop sees the other by its own address, as if they shared a network.**

```
laptop A ~~wifi~~ Pi A (wlan0 10.77.1.1/24) ==== cable ==== Pi B (wlan0 10.77.2.1/24) ~~wifi~~ laptop B
                       eth0 172.31.250.11              eth0 172.31.250.12
```

## What "like the same LAN" means

The tunnel is **routed IPv4**, not a bridge. The two Wi-Fi networks are different subnets (10.77.1.0/24 and
10.77.2.0/24). Anything that works by IP address works across them: ping, web pages, SSH, file sharing by
address, UDP. These do **not** cross: broadcast discovery (mDNS/Bonjour, the "network neighbourhood" list),
and hostnames unless a DNS or hosts entry exists. The laptops are not in one subnet.

## Switching the VPN on and off

On each Pi, as root, with the Pi's own configuration (`demo-pi-a.toml` or `demo-pi-b.toml`, in
`infra/gateway/`, after generating real keys as the file's header says):

```sh
VPTCTL=/usr/local/bin/vptctl VPT1_MODULE=/path/to/vpt1_foundation.ko \
    infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh up   infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml --wait 20   # start B first
infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh status infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh down   infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
```

`up` loads the module if needed, creates `vpn0`, adds the routes to the other Pi's network, installs the
forwarding firewall and the TCP MSS clamp (`mss-clamp.nft`), and starts `vptctl run`. `down` stops the
controller first, which closes the tunnel at once, then removes `vpn0`, the routes and the clamp, and leaves a
firewall that forwards nothing. Everything about the network comes from the one configuration file through
`vptctl perimeter`.

The policy in the demo configurations is whole-network, in both directions on both Pis: ICMP echo, all TCP
ports and all UDP ports between 10.77.1.0/24 and 10.77.2.0/24, so any address the Pi's DHCP server hands out is
covered. Everything else is denied by the kernel's default-deny ACL. The very large UDP datagram limit still
applies (fragments are dropped; see `AY2_DATAPATH.md`, "Packet size").

## Hosting the laptops' Wi-Fi (untested)

`infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh up|down|render CONFIG` runs hostapd and dnsmasq on the configuration's LAN interface, with
the interface, address and network taken from the same file. DHCP hands out .50 to .200 of the /24 with the Pi as the
default gateway and no DNS. It is separate from `vpt-gateway.sh`, so the network can be up with the VPN off, which is
the "laptops cannot see each other" half of the demo. Needs `hostapd` and `dnsmasq` installed:

```sh
VPT_AP_SSID=demo-a VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE='choose-one' VPT_AP_COUNTRY=IN     infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh up infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
```

The passphrase is read from the environment, written only to a `0600` file under `/run/vpt-ap`, and never printed.

## Evidence

`tests/netns/demo_reachability.py` runs the demo with nothing but `vpt-gateway.sh` and the demo
configurations, on the reference VM (x86-64, 6.18, a long-lived working copy of the image, not the AN1 master).
31 checks:

- Before anything starts, laptop A cannot ping or open a connection to laptop B.
- With both Pis up: both directions work for ping, TCP (the server sees the laptop's own source address) and UDP; the
  second laptop on each side, and a second DHCP-style address on a laptop, work too, as source and as destination.
- With the VPN up, a laptop still cannot reach the cable addresses or an address outside the policy.
- Stopping one Pi closes the tunnel in both directions within a few seconds.
- With both Pis down, a laptop still cannot reach the cable even if the other Pi has a route back (checked by
  giving it one), `vpn0` is gone, and switching the VPN on again restores reachability.

A mutation that removes the "off" firewall makes 2 of these fail. The module unloads with no leaked objects.

## Not covered

- **Wi-Fi hosting and DHCP are written but untested.** `infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh` (below) has never been run on a
  Pi. Only its `render` output is tested (`tests/unit/test_ap_script.py`). No second adapter is needed when each Pi's
  only job is this demo: its built-in radio hosts the network and the Ethernet port carries the cable. The radio
  advertises access-point mode (`PLATFORM_PI5.md`), but it has never been tested as one here, so test that early.
  Install packages and set up the Pi while it still has internet; during the demo reach it by joining its own
  Wi-Fi and using SSH to its address (10.77.1.1 or 10.77.2.1).
- **ARM64 and the Pi:** nothing here has run on a Pi. The module has not been built for 6.18 ARM64 with 16 KiB pages.
- **Firewall:** the full HR1 perimeter (`tools/hr1_perimeter.py`) cannot carry traffic yet, because it requires
  packet marks the kernel does not mint (`HR1.md`). `vpt-gateway.sh` installs a smaller forwarding firewall
  (LAN to `vpn0` for the peers' prefixes, nothing else) and the kernel ACL is the actual authorization. Switch to the
  HR1 perimeter once its hooks land.
- No hitless re-keying: about every 90 seconds a few packets are lost during the key change (`CONTROLLER.md`).
- No systemd unit: `up` starts the controller in the background and `down` stops it.

#   vptctl genkey --out /etc/vpntunnel/gw-a.key     (prints the public key to hand to the other Pi)
# and replace the peer's `public_key`. `lan_interface` is the Wi-Fi access-point interface and
# `underlay_interface` the Ethernet port with the cable to the other Pi.
#
# Start and stop with: infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh up|down THIS_FILE

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Bring one VPT1 gateway up or down. The VPN is "on" while this gateway's controller runs.
     3	#
     4	#   vpt-gateway.sh up     CONFIG.toml [--wait SECONDS]   load the module, create vpn0, routes, the
     5	#                                                        forwarding firewall and the MSS clamp, then
     6	#                                                        start `vptctl run` in the background
     7	#   vpt-gateway.sh down   CONFIG.toml                    stop the controller (the tunnel closes at
     8	#                                                        once), remove vpn0, the routes and the MSS
     9	#                                                        clamp, and leave a forward-nothing firewall
    10	#   vpt-gateway.sh status CONFIG.toml                    one line: on / off
    11	#
    12	# Run as root on the gateway (a Pi, or inside a network namespace: `ip netns exec NS ...`).
    13	#
    14	# Environment:
    15	#   VPTCTL        path to the vptctl binary                    (default: vptctl in PATH)
    16	#   VPT1_MODULE   path to vpt1_foundation.ko, loaded only if the module is not loaded yet
    17	#   VPT_RUN_DIR   pid file and controller log directory        (default: /run/vpt-gateway)
    18	#
    19	# Everything the script needs to know about the network comes from CONFIG.toml through
    20	# `vptctl perimeter`: the LAN interface and the peers' prefixes. There is no second copy to drift.
    21	#
    22	# Firewall: the full HR1 perimeter (tools/hr1_perimeter.py) cannot carry traffic yet, because it
    23	# requires packet marks that the kernel does not mint (docs/HR1.md, "not implemented"). This
    24	# script installs a smaller forwarding firewall instead: LAN <-> vpn0 for the peers' prefixes and
    25	# nothing else, so a LAN host can never be forwarded to the underlay. The kernel's own ACL (the
    26	# [[rule]] sections of the config) remains the authorization; this firewall is defence in depth.
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	
    29	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    30	VPTCTL="${VPTCTL:-vptctl}"
    31	RUN_DIR="${VPT_RUN_DIR:-/run/vpt-gateway}"
    32	DEVICE=vpn0
    33	TABLE=vpt_gateway
    34	
    35	usage() {
    36	    sed -n '2,12p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2
    37	    exit 2
    38	}
    39	
    40	[ "$#" -ge 2 ] || usage
    41	ACTION=$1
    42	CONFIG=$2
    43	shift 2
    44	WAIT=0
    45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    46	    case "$1" in
    47	    --wait) WAIT=${2:?--wait needs a number of seconds}; shift 2 ;;
    48	    *) usage ;;
    49	    esac
    50	done
    51	
    52	[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: run as root" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	[ -r "${CONFIG}" ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: cannot read ${CONFIG}" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	command -v "${VPTCTL}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x "${VPTCTL}" ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: vptctl not found (set VPTCTL)" >&2; exit 2; }
    55	
    56	PIDFILE="${RUN_DIR}/controller.pid"
    57	LOGFILE="${RUN_DIR}/controller.log"
    58	
    59	# `vptctl perimeter` validates the whole configuration and prints the LAN interface and the
    60	# peers' prefixes; nothing else is read from the file here.
    61	projection() {
    62	    "${VPTCTL}" perimeter "${CONFIG}"
    63	}
    64	LAN_IF=""
    65	PREFIXES=""
    66	load_projection() {
    67	    local json
    68	    json=$(projection) || { echo "vpt-gateway: configuration rejected" >&2; exit 2; }
    69	    LAN_IF=$(printf '%s' "${json}" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["lan"]["interface"])')
    70	    PREFIXES=$(printf '%s' "${json}" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(" ".join(p for peer in d["peers"] for p in peer["prefixes"]))')
    71	}
    72	
    73	controller_pid() {
    74	    local pid
    75	    [ -r "${PIDFILE}" ] || return 1
    76	    pid=$(cat "${PIDFILE}")
    77	    [ -n "${pid}" ] && kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null && grep -q vptctl "/proc/${pid}/cmdline" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    78	    echo "${pid}"
    79	}
    80	
    81	stop_controller() {
    82	    local pid i
    83	    pid=$(controller_pid) || return 0
    84	    kill -TERM "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    85	    for i in $(seq 1 50); do
    86	        kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || break
    87	        sleep 0.1
    88	    done
    89	    kill -KILL "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    90	    rm -f "${PIDFILE}"
    91	}
    92	
    93	remove_network() {
    94	    nft delete table inet "${TABLE}" 2>/dev/null || true
    95	    nft delete table inet vpt_mss 2>/dev/null || true
    96	    ip link del "${DEVICE}" 2>/dev/null || true # takes its routes with it
    97	}
    98	
    99	# The "off" state: the gateway forwards nothing, so a LAN host cannot reach the underlay or
   100	# anything else through it. (Without this table the kernel would still forward LAN traffic to the
   101	# cable subnet.)
   102	install_isolation() {
   103	    nft -f - <<EOF
   104	table inet ${TABLE} {
   105		chain forward {
   106			type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
   107		}
   108	}
   109	EOF
   110	}
   111	
   112	case "${ACTION}" in
   113	status)
   114	    if controller_pid >/dev/null; then echo "vpt-gateway: on"; else echo "vpt-gateway: off"; fi
   115	    ;;
   116	down)
   117	    # The controller first: closing its socket closes admission at once (fail closed), then the
   118	    # routes and firewall go. The kernel module stays loaded.
   119	    stop_controller
   120	    remove_network
   121	    install_isolation
   122	    echo "vpt-gateway: off"
   123	    ;;
   124	up)
   125	    load_projection
   126	    ip link show "${LAN_IF}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vpt-gateway: no interface ${LAN_IF}" >&2; exit 2; }
   127	    stop_controller
   128	    remove_network
   129	    mkdir -p "${RUN_DIR}"
   130	    chmod 700 "${RUN_DIR}"
   131	    : >"${LOGFILE}"
   132	
   133	    if ! lsmod | grep -q '^vpt1_foundation '; then
   134	        [ -n "${VPT1_MODULE:-}" ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: module not loaded and VPT1_MODULE not set" >&2; exit 2; }
   135	        modprobe chacha20poly1305
   136	        modprobe -q udp_tunnel || true
   137	        insmod "${VPT1_MODULE}"
   138	    fi
   139	
   140	    ip link add "${DEVICE}" type vpt1_ay1
   141	    ip link set "${DEVICE}" up
   142	    sysctl -q -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
   143	    # The gateway forwards between a LAN interface and vpn0; the reverse path is not the
   144	    # interface the packet arrived on, so strict reverse-path filtering would drop it.
   145	    sysctl -q -w "net.ipv4.conf.${DEVICE}.rp_filter=0"
   146	    sysctl -q -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0
   147	    for prefix in ${PREFIXES}; do
   148	        ip route add "${prefix}" dev "${DEVICE}"
   149	    done
   150	
   151	    set_text="$(echo "${PREFIXES}" | sed 's/ /, /g')"
   152	    nft -f - <<EOF
   153	table inet ${TABLE} {
   154		chain forward {
   155			type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
   156			iifname "${LAN_IF}" oifname "${DEVICE}" ip daddr { ${set_text} } accept
   157			iifname "${DEVICE}" oifname "${LAN_IF}" ip saddr { ${set_text} } accept
   158		}
   159	}
   160	EOF
   161	    nft -f "${HERE}/mss-clamp.nft"
   162	
   163	    nohup "${VPTCTL}" run "${CONFIG}" --device "${DEVICE}" >>"${LOGFILE}" 2>&1 </dev/null &
   164	    echo $! >"${PIDFILE}"
   165	    disown || true
   166	
   167	    if [ "${WAIT}" -gt 0 ]; then
   168	        for _ in $(seq 1 $((WAIT * 4))); do
   169	            if grep -q 'established' "${LOGFILE}" 2>/dev/null; then
   170	                echo "vpt-gateway: on (tunnel established)"
   171	                exit 0
   172	            fi
   173	            controller_pid >/dev/null || { echo "vpt-gateway: controller exited; see ${LOGFILE}" >&2; tail -5 "${LOGFILE}" >&2; exit 1; }
   174	            sleep 0.25
   175	        done
   176	        echo "vpt-gateway: controller running, tunnel not established after ${WAIT}s (peer down?)" >&2
   177	        exit 1
   178	    fi
   179	    echo "vpt-gateway: on (controller started; log ${LOGFILE})"
   180	    ;;
   181	*)
   182	    usage
   183	    ;;
   184	esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run every kernel-side test of this repository inside a disposable Linux 6.18 VM.
#
# GitHub-hosted runners have no 6.18 headers and cannot load modules, so this suite
# cannot run in the hosted CI lane. It is the single command a self-hosted or
# disposable-VM job (AN3) runs, and the one to run by hand on the reference VM:
#
#   sudo VPT1_DISPOSABLE_VM=yes VPTCTL=/path/to/vptctl tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh
#
# VPTCTL is optional: with a vptctl binary (cargo build --release in control/) the suite also
# runs the controller end to end; without it that step is reported as SKIP.
#
# It builds a release and a debug (VPT1_DEBUG=1) tree, loads each unit-test module and
# requires its PASS line, runs the end-to-end Generic Netlink test and the two-gateway
# data-path test against both builds, the AY1 smoke script, checks the kernel log for faults, and fails on any leak
# report at unload. Module load and unload are guest-global: never run it on a developer
# machine.
set -uo pipefail

if [ "${VPT1_DISPOSABLE_VM:-}" != "yes" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: set VPT1_DISPOSABLE_VM=yes to confirm this is a disposable VM." >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: run as root." >&2
    exit 2
fi
case "$(uname -r)" in
6.18.*) ;;
*) echo "ERROR: kernel $(uname -r) is not 6.18.y." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "${ROOT}"
FAIL=0
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*" >&2; FAIL=1; }

modprobe chacha20poly1305 || { echo "ERROR: chacha20poly1305 provider unavailable." >&2; exit 2; }
modprobe -q udp_tunnel || true

# A hung module init cannot be unloaded and needs a reboot, so every insmod is bounded
# and a timeout is reported loudly instead of waiting forever.
load() { # MODULE.ko
    timeout 120 insmod "$1"
    local rc=$?
    if [ "${rc}" -eq 124 ]; then
        echo "FATAL: insmod $1 timed out; the guest needs a reboot before further runs." >&2
        exit 3
    fi
    return "${rc}"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# UNTESTED. Host the laptops' Wi-Fi network on a Pi: an access point (hostapd) and DHCP (dnsmasq)
     3	# on the gateway's LAN interface, using the address in the gateway configuration.
     4	#
     5	#   vpt-ap.sh up      CONFIG.toml     start the access point and DHCP on the LAN interface
     6	#   vpt-ap.sh down    CONFIG.toml     stop both and clear the LAN interface address
     7	#   vpt-ap.sh render  CONFIG.toml     print the hostapd and dnsmasq settings, change nothing
     8	#
     9	# This is separate from vpt-gateway.sh (the VPN) so the network can be up with the VPN off, which is
    10	# the "laptops cannot see each other" half of the demo. It has not been run on a Pi: no Pi has
    11	# been available. `render` is covered by tests/unit/test_ap_script.py; `up` and `down` are not.
    12	#
    13	# Environment:
    14	#   VPT_AP_SSID         network name                          (default: vpt-demo-<lan network>)
    15	#   VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE   WPA2 passphrase, 8 to 63 characters   (required for up; never stored here)
    16	#   VPT_AP_COUNTRY      two-letter regulatory country code    (required for up)
    17	#   VPT_AP_CHANNEL      2.4 GHz channel                       (default: 6)
    18	#   VPTCTL              path to the vptctl binary             (default: vptctl in PATH)
    19	#   VPT_RUN_DIR         generated files and pid files         (default: /run/vpt-ap)
    20	#
    21	# The interface, its address and the DHCP range (.50 to .200 of the LAN /24, with the Pi as the
    22	# default gateway and no DNS server handed out) come from the configuration through
    23	# `vptctl perimeter`. Needs: hostapd, dnsmasq, python3, iproute2. NetworkManager is told to leave
    24	# the interface alone if it is running.
    25	set -euo pipefail
    26	
    27	VPTCTL="${VPTCTL:-vptctl}"
    28	RUN_DIR="${VPT_AP_RUN_DIR:-${VPT_RUN_DIR:-/run/vpt-ap}}"
    29	CHANNEL="${VPT_AP_CHANNEL:-6}"
    30	
    31	usage() {
    32	    sed -n '2,12p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2
    33	    exit 2
    34	}
    35	
    36	[ "$#" -eq 2 ] || usage
    37	ACTION=$1
    38	CONFIG=$2
    39	case "${ACTION}" in up | down | render) ;; *) usage ;; esac
    40	
    41	[ -r "${CONFIG}" ] || { echo "vpt-ap: cannot read ${CONFIG}" >&2; exit 2; }
    42	command -v "${VPTCTL}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x "${VPTCTL}" ] || { echo "vpt-ap: vptctl not found (set VPTCTL)" >&2; exit 2; }
    43	if [ "${ACTION}" != render ] && [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    44	    echo "vpt-ap: run as root" >&2
    45	    exit 2
    46	fi
    47	
    48	# One python call: interface, address, prefix length, network, DHCP range and mask.
    49	fields=$("${VPTCTL}" perimeter "${CONFIG}" | python3 -c '
    50	import ipaddress, json, sys
    51	lan = json.load(sys.stdin)["lan"]
    52	iface = ipaddress.ip_interface(lan["address"])
    53	net = iface.network
    54	if net.prefixlen > 24:
    55	    sys.exit("LAN network %s is too small for the DHCP range" % net)
    56	first, last = net.network_address + 50, net.network_address + 200
    57	print(lan["interface"], iface.ip, net.prefixlen, net, first, last, net.netmask)
    58	') || { echo "vpt-ap: configuration rejected" >&2; exit 2; }
    59	read -r LAN_IF LAN_IP LAN_PREFIX LAN_NET RANGE_FIRST RANGE_LAST NETMASK <<<"${fields}"
    60	
    61	SSID="${VPT_AP_SSID:-vpt-demo-${LAN_NET%/*}}"
    62	HOSTAPD_CONF="${RUN_DIR}/hostapd.conf"
    63	HOSTAPD_PID="${RUN_DIR}/hostapd.pid"
    64	DNSMASQ_PID="${RUN_DIR}/dnsmasq.pid"
    65	
    66	# Never put the passphrase in a rendered listing.
    67	render_hostapd() {
    68	    local pass=$1
    69	    cat <<EOF
    70	interface=${LAN_IF}
    71	driver=nl80211
    72	ssid=${SSID}
    73	country_code=${VPT_AP_COUNTRY:-XX}
    74	hw_mode=g
    75	channel=${CHANNEL}
    76	wmm_enabled=1
    77	auth_algs=1
    78	wpa=2
    79	wpa_key_mgmt=WPA-PSK
    80	rsn_pairwise=CCMP
    81	wpa_passphrase=${pass}
    82	EOF
    83	}
    84	
    85	render_dnsmasq_args() {
    86	    cat <<EOF
    87	--conf-file=/dev/null
    88	--interface=${LAN_IF}
    89	--bind-interfaces
    90	--except-interface=lo
    91	--port=0
    92	--dhcp-range=${RANGE_FIRST},${RANGE_LAST},${NETMASK},12h
    93	--dhcp-option=option:router,${LAN_IP}
    94	--dhcp-option=option:dns-server
    95	--dhcp-authoritative
    96	--pid-file=${DNSMASQ_PID}
    97	EOF
    98	}
    99	
   100	kill_pid() {
   101	    local file=$1 pid
   102	    [ -r "${file}" ] || return 0
   103	    pid=$(cat "${file}")
   104	    [ -n "${pid}" ] && kill -TERM "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
   105	    rm -f "${file}"
   106	}
   107	
   108	case "${ACTION}" in
   109	render)
   110	    echo "# interface ${LAN_IF}, address ${LAN_IP}/${LAN_PREFIX}, network ${LAN_NET}"
   111	    echo "# hostapd.conf"
   112	    render_hostapd "<passphrase>"
   113	    echo "# dnsmasq arguments"
   114	    render_dnsmasq_args
   115	    ;;
   116	down)
   117	    kill_pid "${HOSTAPD_PID}"
   118	    kill_pid "${DNSMASQ_PID}"
   119	    rm -f "${HOSTAPD_CONF}"
   120	    ip addr flush dev "${LAN_IF}" 2>/dev/null || true
   121	    echo "vpt-ap: down"
   122	    ;;
   123	up)
   124	    pass="${VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE:-}"
   125	    [ "${#pass}" -ge 8 ] && [ "${#pass}" -le 63 ] || { echo "vpt-ap: set VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE (8 to 63 characters)" >&2; exit 2; }
   126	    [[ "${VPT_AP_COUNTRY:-}" =~ ^[A-Z]{2}$ ]] || { echo "vpt-ap: set VPT_AP_COUNTRY to a two-letter code, e.g. IN" >&2; exit 2; }
   127	    command -v hostapd >/dev/null && command -v dnsmasq >/dev/null || { echo "vpt-ap: hostapd and dnsmasq must be installed" >&2; exit 2; }
   128	    ip link show "${LAN_IF}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vpt-ap: no interface ${LAN_IF}" >&2; exit 2; }
   129	
   130	    kill_pid "${HOSTAPD_PID}"
   131	    kill_pid "${DNSMASQ_PID}"
   132	    mkdir -p "${RUN_DIR}"
   133	    chmod 700 "${RUN_DIR}"
   134	    (umask 077 && render_hostapd "${pass}" >"${HOSTAPD_CONF}")
   135	
   136	    command -v rfkill >/dev/null && rfkill unblock wifi || true
   137	    command -v nmcli >/dev/null && nmcli device set "${LAN_IF}" managed no 2>/dev/null || true
   138	    ip addr flush dev "${LAN_IF}"
   139	    ip addr add "${LAN_IP}/${LAN_PREFIX}" dev "${LAN_IF}"
   140	    ip link set "${LAN_IF}" up
   141	
   142	    hostapd -B -P "${HOSTAPD_PID}" "${HOSTAPD_CONF}"
   143	    mapfile -t args < <(render_dnsmasq_args)
   144	    dnsmasq "${args[@]}"
   145	    echo "vpt-ap: up (SSID ${SSID} on ${LAN_IF}, ${LAN_IP}/${LAN_PREFIX}, DHCP ${RANGE_FIRST} to ${RANGE_LAST})"
   146	    ;;
   147	esac

class Pi:
    """One gateway driven only through the bring-up script."""

    def __init__(self, site, config, tmp):
        self.site, self.config = site, config
        self.env = {"VPTCTL": VPTCTL, "VPT_RUN_DIR": os.path.join(tmp, f"run-{site}"), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}

    def script(self, action, *extra):
        return subprocess.run(["ip", "netns", "exec", ns(self.site), "env"] + [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in self.env.items()]
                              + ["bash", SCRIPT, action, self.config, *extra],
                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)

    def log(self):
        try:
            return open(os.path.join(self.env["VPT_RUN_DIR"], "controller.log")).read()
        except OSError:
            return ""


def make_config(template, site, tmp, own_key, peer_pub):
    text = open(os.path.join(REPO, "infra/gateway", template)).read()
    text = re.sub(r'private_key_file = ".*"', f'private_key_file = "{own_key}"', text)
    text = text.replace('"wlan0"', f'"veth_gw{site}_lan"').replace('"eth0"', f'"veth_gw{site}_out"')
    text = re.sub(r'public_key = "[0-9a-f]{64}"', f'public_key = "{peer_pub}"', text)
    path = os.path.join(tmp, f"{template}")
    open(path, "w").write(text)
    return path


def main():
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        sys.exit("run as root in a disposable VM")
    if not VPTCTL or not os.path.exists(VPTCTL):
        sys.exit("set VPTCTL to the vptctl binary")
    r = run("bash", os.path.join(HERE, "n1_fixture.sh"), "setup", D.RUN)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"fixture setup failed: {r.stderr or r.stdout}")
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="demo_")
    os.chmod(tmp, 0o700)
    servers = []
    pis = []
    try:
        keys, pubs = {}, {}
        for who in ("a", "b"):
            keys[who] = os.path.join(tmp, f"{who}.key")
            out = run(VPTCTL, "genkey", "--out", keys[who]).stdout
            pubs[who] = re.search(r"public_key\s+([0-9a-f]{64})", out).group(1)
        cfg_a = make_config("demo-pi-a.toml", "a", tmp, keys["a"], pubs["b"])
        cfg_b = make_config("demo-pi-b.toml", "b", tmp, keys["b"], pubs["a"])
        for cfg in (cfg_a, cfg_b):
            check("demo-config-validates", run(VPTCTL, "check-config", cfg, "--with-key").returncode == 0,
                  run(VPTCTL, "check-config", cfg, "--with-key").stderr[-300:])
        pi_a, pi_b = Pi("gwa", cfg_a, tmp), Pi("gwb", cfg_b, tmp)
        pis += [pi_a, pi_b]

        # The laptops: a default route through their Pi, and a second ("DHCP") address each.
        for h, gw in (("ha", "10.77.1.1"), ("ha2", "10.77.1.1"), ("hb", "10.77.2.1"), ("hb2", "10.77.2.1")):
            host(h, "ip", "route", "replace", "default", "via", gw)
        host("ha", "ip", "addr", "add", "10.77.1.57/24", "dev", "veth_ha")
        host("hb", "ip", "addr", "add", "10.77.2.88/24", "dev", "veth_hb")

        for h, addr, port, sid in (("hb", "10.77.2.88", 8080, "laptop-b"), ("ha", "10.77.1.57", 8081, "laptop-a")):
            servers.append(subprocess.Popen(
                ["ip", "netns", "exec", ns(h), sys.executable, os.path.join(REPO, "tools/oracles/http_server.py"),
                 "--host", addr, "--port", str(port), "--server-id", sid],
                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL))
        time.sleep(0.6)

        def http(src, url, server_id, client_ip, timeout="3"):
            r = host(src, sys.executable, os.path.join(REPO, "tools/oracles/http_client.py"), url,
                     "--expect-server", server_id, "--expect-client-ip", client_ip, "--timeout", timeout)
            return r.returncode == 0, r.stdout[-200:]

        def udp_echo(src, bind_addr, dst, dst_ns):
            srv = subprocess.Popen(["ip", "netns", "exec", ns(dst_ns), sys.executable, "-c",
                                    "import socket;s=socket.socket(2,2);s.bind(('%s',5353));s.settimeout(4)\n"
                                    "d,a=s.recvfrom(2000);s.sendto(d.upper(),a)" % dst],
                                   stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            time.sleep(0.5)
            code = ("import socket;s=socket.socket(2,2);s.bind(('%s',0));s.settimeout(3)\n"
                    "s.sendto(b'hello',('%s',5353));print(s.recvfrom(100)[0].decode())" % (bind_addr, dst))
            r = host(src, sys.executable, "-c", code)
            srv.terminate()
            return r.stdout.strip() == "HELLO"

        # 1. Nothing started: the laptops cannot see each other.
        check("never-started-ping-fails", not ping("ha", "10.77.2.10"))
        check("never-started-tcp-fails", not http("ha", "http://10.77.2.88:8080", "laptop-b", "10.77.1.57", "1.5")[0])

        # 2. Both Pis on.
        out_b = pi_b.script("up")
        check("pi-b-up", out_b.returncode == 0, out_b.stdout + out_b.stderr)
        out_a = pi_a.script("up", "--wait", "20")
        check("pi-a-up-and-established", out_a.returncode == 0, out_a.stdout + out_a.stderr + pi_a.log()[-300:])
        check("status-reports-on", "on" in pi_a.script("status").stdout)
        check("laptop-a-reaches-laptop-b", wait_for(lambda: ping("ha", "10.77.2.10"), 10))
        check("laptop-b-reaches-laptop-a", ping("hb", "10.77.1.10"))
        check("second-laptops-too", ping("ha2", "10.77.2.11") and ping("hb2", "10.77.1.11"))
        check("dhcp-style-extra-addresses-too", ping("ha", "10.77.2.88") and ping("hb", "10.77.1.57"))
        check("extra-address-as-the-source-too",
              host("ha", "ping", "-c", "2", "-W", "1", "-I", "10.77.1.57", "10.77.2.88").returncode == 0)
        ok, detail = http("ha", "http://10.77.2.88:8080", "laptop-b", "10.77.1.10")
        check("a-browses-b-and-b-sees-its-address", ok, detail)
        ok, detail = http("hb", "http://10.77.1.57:8081", "laptop-a", "10.77.2.10")
        check("b-browses-a-and-a-sees-its-address", ok, detail)
        check("udp-both-ways", udp_echo("ha", "10.77.1.57", "10.77.2.88", "hb"))

        # 3. What is still not reachable while the VPN is on.
        check("laptop-cannot-reach-the-cable-address", not ping("ha", "172.31.250.12", 1))
        check("laptop-cannot-reach-the-other-pis-underlay-via-a-route", not ping("hb", "172.31.250.11", 1))
        check("unowned-address-not-reachable", not ping("ha", "10.77.3.10", 1))

        # 4. One Pi switched off: the tunnel closes at once in both directions.
        check("a-down", pi_a.script("down").returncode == 0)
        check("status-reports-off", "off" in pi_a.script("status").stdout)
        check("closes-a-to-b", wait_for(lambda: not ping("ha", "10.77.2.10", 1), 4))
        check("closes-b-to-a", not ping("hb", "10.77.1.10", 1))

        # 5. Both off: still isolated, including from the cable.
        check("b-down", pi_b.script("down").returncode == 0)
        check("both-off-no-laptop-to-laptop", not ping("ha", "10.77.2.10", 1) and not ping("hb", "10.77.1.10", 1))
        # Give the other Pi a route back, so a leaked packet would really get an answer.
        host("gwb", "ip", "route", "add", "10.77.1.0/24", "via", "172.31.250.11")
        check("both-off-laptop-cannot-reach-the-cable", not ping("ha", "172.31.250.12", 1))
        check("both-off-gateway-forwards-nothing",

                              + ["bash", SCRIPT, action, self.config, *extra],
                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)

"""Scratch probe (not part of the repo): how long does the demo take to recover when ONE Pi

import re
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import demo_reachability as R  # noqa: E402

D = R.D
results = []


def recovery(label, limit, probe):
    start = time.time()
    while time.time() - start < limit:
        if probe():
            took = time.time() - start
            results.append((label, round(took, 1), "recovered"))
            print(f"RESULT {label}: recovered after {took:.1f}s", flush=True)
            return took
        time.sleep(0.5)
    results.append((label, limit, "NOT recovered within limit"))
    print(f"RESULT {label}: NOT recovered within {limit}s", flush=True)
    return None


def a_to_b():
    return R.ping("ha", "10.77.2.10", 1, 1)


def b_to_a():
    return R.ping("hb", "10.77.1.10", 1, 1)


def both():
    return a_to_b() and b_to_a()


def main():
    r = R.run("bash", os.path.join(R.HERE, "n1_fixture.sh"), "setup", D.RUN)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"fixture setup failed: {r.stderr or r.stdout}")
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="probe_")
    os.chmod(tmp, 0o700)
    pis = []
    try:

        for who in ("a", "b"):

            pubs[who] = re.search(r"public_key\s+([0-9a-f]{64})", out).group(1)
        cfg_a = R.make_config("demo-pi-a.toml", "a", tmp, keys["a"], pubs["b"])
        cfg_b = R.make_config("demo-pi-b.toml", "b", tmp, keys["b"], pubs["a"])
        pi_a, pi_b = R.Pi("gwa", cfg_a, tmp), R.Pi("gwb", cfg_b, tmp)
        pis += [pi_a, pi_b]
        for h, gw in (("ha", "10.77.1.1"), ("hb", "10.77.2.1")):
            R.host(h, "ip", "route", "replace", "default", "via", gw)

        print("## baseline: B first, then A (the documented order)", flush=True)
        assert pi_b.script("up").returncode == 0
        out = pi_a.script("up", "--wait", "20")
        assert out.returncode == 0, out.stdout + out.stderr
        recovery("baseline both directions", 20, both)

        print("## 1. A (initiator) restarts; B keeps running", flush=True)
        pi_a.script("down")
        out = pi_a.script("up", "--wait", "30")
        print("   A up:", (out.stdout + out.stderr).strip()[:120], flush=True)
        recovery("1. A restarted, B untouched: a->b", 120, a_to_b)
        recovery("1. A restarted, B untouched: b->a", 30, b_to_a)

        print("## 2. B (responder) restarts; A keeps running", flush=True)
        pi_b.script("down")
        pi_b.script("up")
        recovery("2. B restarted, A untouched: a->b", 180, a_to_b)
        recovery("2. B restarted, A untouched: b->a", 30, b_to_a)

        print("## 3. A's controller is killed with SIGKILL (power loss), then comes back", flush=True)
        pid = int(open(os.path.join(pi_a.env["VPT_RUN_DIR"], "controller.pid")).read())

        print("   A up:", (out.stdout + out.stderr).strip()[:120], flush=True)
        recovery("3. A killed and restarted: a->b", 120, a_to_b)

        print("## 4. opposite start order: both down, A first, B 5 s later", flush=True)

        recovery("4. A started 5s before B: a->b", 120, a_to_b)
        recovery("4. A started 5s before B: b->a", 30, b_to_a)

        print("## 5. A started long before B: 40 s head start", flush=True)
        pi_a.script("down")
        pi_b.script("down")
        time.sleep(1)
        pi_a.script("up")
        time.sleep(40)
        print("   A's log tail:", pi_a.log()[-300:].replace("\n", " | "), flush=True)
        assert pi_b.script("up").returncode == 0
        recovery("5. A started 40s before B: a->b", 150, a_to_b)
    finally:

    main()

def recovery(label, limit, probe):
    start = time.time()
    while time.time() - start < limit:
        if probe():
            took = time.time() - start
            results.append((label, round(took, 1), "recovered"))
            print(f"RESULT {label}: recovered after {took:.1f}s", flush=True)
            return took
        time.sleep(0.5)
    results.append((label, limit, "NOT recovered within limit"))
    print(f"RESULT {label}: NOT recovered within {limit}s", flush=True)
    return None


def a_to_b():
    return R.ping("ha", "10.77.2.10", 1, 1)


def b_to_a():
    return R.ping("hb", "10.77.1.10", 1, 1)


def both():
    return a_to_b() and b_to_a()


def main():
    r = R.run("bash", os.path.join(R.HERE, "n1_fixture.sh"), "setup", D.RUN)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"fixture setup failed: {r.stderr or r.stdout}")
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="probe_")
    os.chmod(tmp, 0o700)
    pis = []
    try:
        keys, pubs = {}, {}
        for who in ("a", "b"):
            keys[who] = os.path.join(tmp, f"{who}.key")
            out = R.run(R.VPTCTL, "genkey", "--out", keys[who]).stdout
            pubs[who] = re.search(r"public_key\s+([0-9a-f]{64})", out).group(1)
        cfg_a = R.make_config("demo-pi-a.toml", "a", tmp, keys["a"], pubs["b"])
        cfg_b = R.make_config("demo-pi-b.toml", "b", tmp, keys["b"], pubs["a"])
        pi_a, pi_b = R.Pi("gwa", cfg_a, tmp), R.Pi("gwb", cfg_b, tmp)
        pis += [pi_a, pi_b]
        for h, gw in (("ha", "10.77.1.1"), ("hb", "10.77.2.1")):
            R.host(h, "ip", "route", "replace", "default", "via", gw)

        print("## baseline: B first, then A (the documented order)", flush=True)
        assert pi_b.script("up").returncode == 0
        out = pi_a.script("up", "--wait", "20")
        assert out.returncode == 0, out.stdout + out.stderr
        recovery("baseline both directions", 20, both)

        print("## 1. A (initiator) restarts; B keeps running", flush=True)
        pi_a.script("down")
        out = pi_a.script("up", "--wait", "30")
        print("   A up:", (out.stdout + out.stderr).strip()[:120], flush=True)
        recovery("1. A restarted, B untouched: a->b", 120, a_to_b)
        recovery("1. A restarted, B untouched: b->a", 30, b_to_a)

        print("## 2. B (responder) restarts; A keeps running", flush=True)
        pi_b.script("down")
        pi_b.script("up")
        recovery("2. B restarted, A untouched: a->b", 180, a_to_b)
        recovery("2. B restarted, A untouched: b->a", 30, b_to_a)

        print("## 3. A's controller is killed with SIGKILL (power loss), then comes back", flush=True)
        pid = int(open(os.path.join(pi_a.env["VPT_RUN_DIR"], "controller.pid")).read())
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        time.sleep(1.5)
        print("   a->b right after the kill (expect failure):", a_to_b(), flush=True)
        out = pi_a.script("up", "--wait", "30")
        print("   A up:", (out.stdout + out.stderr).strip()[:120], flush=True)
        recovery("3. A killed and restarted: a->b", 120, a_to_b)

        print("## 4. opposite start order: both down, A first, B 5 s later", flush=True)
        pi_a.script("down")
        pi_b.script("down")
        time.sleep(1)
        out = pi_a.script("up")  # no --wait: B is not there yet
        print("   A up (no wait):", (out.stdout + out.stderr).strip()[:100], flush=True)
        time.sleep(5)
        assert pi_b.script("up").returncode == 0
        recovery("4. A started 5s before B: a->b", 120, a_to_b)
        recovery("4. A started 5s before B: b->a", 30, b_to_a)

        print("## 5. A started long before B: 40 s head start", flush=True)
        pi_a.script("down")
        pi_b.script("down")
        time.sleep(1)
        pi_a.script("up")
        time.sleep(40)
        print("   A's log tail:", pi_a.log()[-300:].replace("\n", " | "), flush=True)
        assert pi_b.script("up").returncode == 0
        recovery("5. A started 40s before B: a->b", 150, a_to_b)
    finally:
        for p in pis:
            p.script("down")
        R.run("bash", os.path.join(R.HERE, "n1_fixture.sh"), "teardown", D.RUN)
    print("SUMMARY")
    for label, secs, status in results:
        print(f"  {label:50s} {secs:>6}s  {status}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
