b=s.index("        # 3. Changes that must be refused")
new='''        # 1. Policy-only change while traffic runs: one more rule. Both gateways enforce the policy (the
        # sender before the tunnel, the receiver after it), so the port opens only when both have it.
        # Nothing may be lost or re-keyed.
        inits0, tx0 = inits(), CT.counters("gwa")["TX_EXCHANGE"]
        ping = subprocess.Popen(["ip", "netns", "exec", D.NS["ha"], "ping", "-c", "200", "-i", "0.05", "-W", "1",
                                 "10.77.2.10"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
        time.sleep(1.5)
        write_atomic(cfg_a, base_a + EXTRA_RULE)
        check("rule-added-is-reloaded-as-revision-2",
              CT.wait_for(lambda: log_has("reloaded as revision 2"), 8), ca.text()[-400:])
        check("one-gateway-alone-does-not-open-the-port", not http(9999))
        write_atomic(cfg_b, base_b + EXTRA_RULE)
        check("the-responder-reloads-its-own-file",
              CT.wait_for(lambda: "reloaded as revision 2" in cb.text(), 8), cb.text()[-400:])
        m = re.search(r"(\\d+) packets transmitted, (\\d+) received", ping.communicate(timeout=60)[0])
        lost = int(m[1]) - int(m[2]) if m else 999
        check("no-packet-lost-across-a-policy-only-reload", lost == 0, f"{lost} lost")
        for who, ctl in (("initiator", ca), ("responder", cb)):
            check(f"policy-only-reload-kept-the-{who}-peer",
                  "kept [1], replaced [], added [], removed []" in ctl.text(), ctl.text()[-300:])
        check("policy-only-reload-started-no-exchange", inits() == inits0 and
              CT.counters("gwa")["TX_EXCHANGE"] == tx0, f"{inits0}->{inits()}")
        check("the-new-rule-is-enforced-once-both-have-it", http(9999))
        check("the-old-rule-still-works", http(8080))

        # 2. The same change reversed: a revoked rule stops being enforced at once, on the first
        # gateway that revokes it.
        write_atomic(cfg_a, base_a)
        check("rule-removed-is-reloaded-as-revision-3",
              CT.wait_for(lambda: log_has("reloaded as revision 3"), 8), ca.text()[-400:])
        check("the-revoked-rule-is-denied-at-once", not http(9999))
        write_atomic(cfg_b, base_b)
        check("the-responder-revokes-too",
              CT.wait_for(lambda: "reloaded as revision 3" in cb.text(), 8), cb.text()[-400:])
        check("traffic-the-rules-still-allow-works", http(8080) and CT.ping_ok())
        check("revoking-started-no-exchange", inits() == inits0, f"{inits0}->{inits()}")

'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]

# remove old step 5 (responder reload) block
c=s.index("        # 5. The responder follows a reload too")
d=s.index("        faults = D.sh(")
s=s[:c]+s[d:]

Guest `6.18.0-vpt1-ref` x86-64 (a long-lived working copy of the reference image, not the AN1 master).

- **Controller unit tests** (`cargo test --locked`, no kernel; 90 library tests pass): the state machine
  through an in-memory port (mirrored keys and locators, a lost INIT retransmitted with the same bytes, a
  lost RESPONSE answered from the cache with one generation installed, forged messages changing nothing,
  timeout and backoff, re-establishment with fresh keys, a stale kernel incarnation refreshed once), and
  the SNAPSHOT encoder, request builders and STATUS/event decoders against the exact record layouts.
- **`tests/netns/ay2_controller.py`, 21 assertions:** two `vptctl run` processes on the N1 fixture and
  nothing else configures anything. The tunnel comes up; ping and HTTP cross it with the original source;
  the underlay carries INIT, RESPONSE and RECORD datagrams and no private packet, no request ID and no
  static key in the clear; a denied port never arrives; the initiator re-keys every 8 s (test setting)
  and 2000 pings each way over 20 s, with 20 ms of delay on the underlay, lose nothing; a forged INIT is rejected and changes nothing; killing the
  controller stops traffic within 3 s (it releases the lease); restarting it brings the tunnel back.
  A mutation that swaps the key directions on the initiator only makes 7 assertions fail.
- Kernel: `EXCHANGE_TX` sends only a whole INIT (224 bytes, zero locator) or RESPONSE (176 bytes, nonzero
  locator) from the bound socket; a malformed one is `-EINVAL`, an unconfigured slot `-ENOENT`.
  `tests/netns/ay2_genl.py` covers these (71 assertions).

## Not covered

- No REKEY_START continuity grant, no activation handshake (CONFIRM/READY/COMMIT), and no liveness PING/PONG. INIT/RESPONSE are the only control messages that exist.
- One configuration revision per session; no live reconfiguration, no staged policy updates, and the
  controller does not install nftables or routes (`infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh` installs the forwarding ruleset; the `vpn0` device and
  routes are created by hand above).
- The kernel, not the controller, should allocate attempt IDs and receive locators per the design; this
  controller picks them (the kernel checks that locators are nonzero and unique in the gateway).
- No daemonization, privilege dropping or core-dump disabling, and no signal handler: stopping the process
  releases the socket, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour.
- Not run: ARM64/Pi 5, macOS (the Linux-only modules are compiled out), long soak, many peers, concurrent
  reconfiguration against live traffic.
prefix; tcp/udp need `ports`, `icmp-echo` forbids them; config ≤ 64 KiB.
The outer UDP port is fixed at 51888 and is not configurable.

**Slot stability.** `slot` is the kernel `PEER_SLOT`. Reordering peers in the
file never changes it. For the same pinned identity, a slot may be kept across
reloads; a slot must not be given to a different identity, endpoint or owned
prefix set without a fresh session under a new peer incarnation, because the
kernel keys incarnations, marks and locks by slot. TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md section
13 calls this kind of reassignment disruptive. Enforcing it during a reload
belongs to the later RJ4 reconciliation work; today the config loader only
validates one file.

## Network summary (`src/network.rs`)
Not done: the activation handshake, the live fragment hook, transactional controller updates and live reconfiguration (RJ4), AN4's campaigns, and the physical two-Pi run (AN5). One Raspberry Pi 5 has passed the kernel suite; Pi A and the two-Pi demo have not run. These slices do not complete the VPN. The x86-64 reference image and fixtures exist

p='docs/CONTROLLER.md'
s=open(p).read()
sec='''## Live reconfiguration

`vptctl run` compares its configuration file with the bytes it started from about once a second (bytes, not a
timestamp, so an editor's write-and-rename works and rewriting identical content is no change). A changed file is
applied to the **running session** as the next revision, with no restart and no new claim:

1. The new file is parsed and validated like the first one. The gateway's own key must be unchanged (a new key
   means a restart), the interfaces must exist, and the snapshot must encode.
2. The kernel validates the snapshot and commits it as revision N+1 (`VALIDATE`, `COMMIT_CONFIG`), and the lease
   is renewed under the new revision.
3. The controller reads `STATUS` and follows the kernel, not its own guess: a slot whose peer incarnation is
   unchanged keeps its exchange state and timers (the kernel keeps a peer only when nothing about it changed,
   `peer_cfg_equal`: role, path MTU, endpoint, key, prefixes); a slot with a new incarnation starts a fresh
   exchange at once; a new slot starts one; a removed slot is dropped with its cached RESPONSE.

Anything refused before or by the kernel (a parse or validation error, a different gateway key, a missing
interface, `-EINVAL`, `-ENOSPC`, `-EBUSY`, `-ENOMEM`) leaves the running configuration and the tunnel as they
were. It is logged once and not retried until the file changes again. A refusal that means the session itself is
gone (lost lease, wrong owner) ends the session as before. The controller never lowers a rule count or rewrites a
snapshot to make it fit.

A change to the **policy** (rules) is hitless in the test: no packet lost, no exchange. A change to the **peer**
(an owned prefix added) is disruptive by the kernel's own classification: the peer is replaced, traffic stops
until the new exchange completes (about a second), then resumes. Both gateways enforce the policy, so a rule
opens a port only once both have it, and revoking it on either closes it at once.

`tests/netns/rj4_reload.py` (31 assertions, in the kernel VM suite): policy-only reload under a 200-ping flow on
both gateways (kept peer, no INIT, no loss), revocation, garbage and a different key refused and logged once,
restoring the running file doing nothing, a peer change followed by a new exchange and traffic. A mutation that
skips `Controller::reconfigure` makes 5 of them fail. The unit tests cover the slot bookkeeping, including a
removed and re-added slot, a role or key that disagrees with the kernel's view, and a replaced responder that
must not replay its old peer's cached RESPONSE.

'''
s=s.replace("## Not covered\n",sec+"## Not covered\n",1)
s=s.replace('''- One configuration revision per session; no live reconfiguration, no staged policy updates, and the
  controller does not install nftables or routes''','''- No multi-facility transaction: the controller changes only the kernel configuration. It does not install
  nftables or routes''')
s=s.replace('''- Not run: ARM64/Pi 5, macOS (the Linux-only modules are compiled out), long soak, many peers, concurrent
  reconfiguration against live traffic.''','''- Reload is a file poll, not a signal or a command, and only the one session's gateway key is fixed for its
  life. A reload that replaces a peer drops that peer's traffic until the new exchange completes. The shared
  `vpn0` MTU is not recomputed when a peer's path MTU changes (the kernel computes it, not the controller).
- Not run: ARM64/Pi 5, macOS (the Linux-only modules are compiled out), long soak, many peers (removal of one of
  several peers is unit-tested only), reload under heavy load.''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='control/README.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''13 calls this kind of reassignment disruptive. Enforcing it during a reload
belongs to the later RJ4 reconciliation work; today the config loader only
validates one file.''','''13 calls this kind of reassignment disruptive. The kernel enforces it: a peer
whose role, path MTU, endpoint, key or prefixes changed is replaced with a new
incarnation, and a running `vptctl run` follows that incarnation on reload
(`docs/CONTROLLER.md`, "Live reconfiguration").''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("transactional controller updates and live reconfiguration (RJ4), AN4's campaigns","multi-facility transactional updates (RJ4: a running controller does reload a changed configuration file as the next kernel revision), AN4's campaigns")

## Behavior changed
`vptctl run` can now change its configuration without a restart. It compares its file with the bytes it started from about once a second and applies a change as the next kernel revision in the same session (`VALIDATE`, `COMMIT_CONFIG` at N+1, lease renewed under N+1). Before this, one revision was committed per session and the only way to change a config was `vpt-gateway.sh down` then `up`.

- **The controller follows the kernel's classification, it does not repeat it.** After the commit it reads `STATUS`. A slot whose peer incarnation is unchanged keeps its exchange state and timers (the kernel keeps a peer only when `peer_cfg_equal` holds: role, path MTU, endpoint, key, prefixes). A replaced or new slot starts a fresh exchange at once; a removed slot is dropped with its cached RESPONSE (`Controller::reconfigure`).
- **Refusals leave everything as it was.** A parse or validation error, a different gateway key (that is a restart), a missing interface, or `-EINVAL`/`-ENOSPC`/`-EBUSY`/`-ENOMEM` from the kernel is logged once and not retried until the file changes. Errors that mean the session is gone (lost lease, wrong owner) still end it. The controller never lowers a rule count or rewrites a snapshot to fit. This is the behavior the #43 contract text asks for.
- The file is read bounded (64 KiB), compared by content (an editor's write-and-rename works; rewriting identical bytes is no change), and read once at session start so the validated bytes are the baseline.

Design sections: TECHNICAL_DESIGN §13 (disruptive vs policy-only), `docs/AY2_CONTRACT.md` (revision/owner-epoch binding). No wire, Netlink or kernel change.

## Tests and environment
- **Unit (12 new):** slot bookkeeping (policy-only keeps session and the 90 s timer, replaced peer starts an exchange, missing or zero incarnation never counts as kept, a role or key that disagrees with the kernel's view starts over, removed and re-added slots, a replaced responder must not replay its old peer's cached RESPONSE) and the watcher (unchanged, changed until applied, rejected not retried, missing file, oversized file, non-UTF-8). Mutations (always keep, never keep, carry the cache over) each fail the intended tests.
- **`tests/netns/rj4_reload.py`, 31 assertions, added to `tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh`:** two real `vptctl run` on the N1 fixture. A policy-only reload during 200 pings loses 0 packets and sends no INIT (no new `TX_EXCHANGE`); one gateway alone does not open a new port (both enforce), both together do; a revoked rule is denied at once; garbage and a different gateway key are refused and logged once; restoring the running file changes nothing; adding an owned prefix makes the kernel replace the peer, a fresh exchange follows and traffic resumes; no kernel fault markers. Skipping `Controller::reconfigure` makes 5 of them fail.
- **Environment:** AN1 reference VM `6.18.0-vpt1-ref` (x86-64, QEMU TCG on an Apple Silicon Mac), release controller and module built in the guest. Also passing there on this head: `ay2_controller.py` (23/23) and `ay4_usage_rekey.py` (7/7). Linux (Lima ARM64 Debian): fmt, locked Clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --locked` (108 lib tests). macOS: fmt, Clippy, 102 tests, doc links.
- **Not run:** the rest of `tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh` (HR/AY unit modules, soak, demo reachability) on this head, debug-kernel configs, ARM64/Pi, a multi-peer reload on the VM (removal of one of several peers is unit-tested only).

## Limitations
- Reload is a file poll, not a signal or a command. A new gateway key still needs a restart.
- A reload that replaces a peer drops that peer's traffic until the new exchange completes (about a second here); that is the kernel's disruptive classification.
- The shared `vpn0` MTU is not recomputed when a peer's path MTU changes (kernel side, see my #41 review).
- This touches `daemon.rs` and `session.rs`, as do #51 (timers) and #52 (RJ5 tests); expect a small rebase in whichever merges second.
EOF

content.text:
PR [#54](https://github.com/Aayush75/VPNTunnel/pull/54) is open for item 5 (live reconfiguration), authored only as rajmodi8905 with no Claude trailers. Item 4 is not started.

**What it does:** `vptctl run` now checks its config file about once a second. A changed file is applied to the running session as the next kernel revision, with no restart. After the commit the controller reads the kernel's `STATUS` and follows the incarnation:
- **Unchanged slot:** the peer keeps its session and timers.
- **Replaced or new slot:** a fresh exchange starts at once.
- **Removed slot:** its state is dropped.

**What it refuses, leaving the tunnel untouched:** a parse or validation error, a different gateway key, a missing interface, or a kernel refusal such as `-EINVAL` or `-ENOSPC`. Each is logged once and not retried until the file changes again. A lost lease still ends the session as before.

**Verified on the reference VM:**
- **New test:** `tests/netns/rj4_reload.py` passes 31/31. A policy-only reload during a 200-ping flow lost nothing and started no exchange. A revoked rule was denied at once. Garbage and a different key were refused. Adding a peer prefix made the kernel replace the peer, a new exchange followed, and traffic resumed.
- **Mutation check:** skipping the controller's reconfigure step fails 5 of those checks.
- **No regression:** `ay2_controller` passes 23/23 and `ay4_usage_rekey` 7/7 on this head.
- **Other checks:** 12 new unit tests. On Linux (Lima) the format check, Clippy and all tests pass, and on macOS they pass too.

- **Both gateways enforce the policy.** A new port opens only once both gateways have the rule. My first version of the test missed this, and it failed until I fixed the test.

import socket

import subprocess

import tempfile

sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import ay2_genl as G  # noqa: E402  (shared netlink helpers)

RUN = f"dp{os.getpid()}"
NS = {n: f"vpt_{RUN}_{n}" for n in ("ha", "gwa", "und", "gwb", "hb")}
ID_A, ID_B = bytes(range(1, 17)), bytes(range(51, 67))
K1, K2 = bytes(range(32)), bytes(range(100, 132))
LOC_A, LOC_B = 0xA1A2A3A4A5A6A7A8, 0xB1B2B3B4B5B6B7B8

# counter ids: reasons 0..13 then events (see vpt1_gateway.h)
C = dict(TX_PACKETS=21, RX_PACKETS=22, TX_NO_ROUTE=23, TX_DROPPED=24, RX_MALFORMED=25,
         RX_UNKNOWN_LOCATOR=26, RX_BAD_SOURCE=27, RX_AUTH_FAIL=28, RX_REPLAY=29,
         RX_POLICY=30, RX_DROPPED=31)

passed = failed = 0


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAIL {name} {detail}")


def sh(*argv, ns=None, timeout=30, check_rc=False):
    cmd = (["ip", "netns", "exec", NS[ns]] if ns else []) + list(argv)
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    if check_rc and r.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{' '.join(cmd)}: {r.stderr.strip()}")
    return r


@contextlib.contextmanager
def netns(name):
    """Create sockets inside a namespace: a socket keeps the namespace it was born in."""
    home = os.open("/proc/self/ns/net", os.O_RDONLY)
    target = os.open(f"/var/run/netns/{NS[name]}", os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.setns(target, os.CLONE_NEWNET)
        yield
    finally:
        os.setns(home, os.CLONE_NEWNET)
        os.close(home)
        os.close(target)

A = dict(IFINDEX=1, CONTROLLER_ID=2, CONFIG_REVISION=3, PEER_SLOT=4,
         PEER_INCARNATION=5, ATTEMPT_ID=6, HANDSHAKE_HASH=7, LOCAL_RX=8,
         REMOTE_RX=9, TX_KEY=10, RX_KEY=11, MODE=12, PARENT_HASH=13,
         EXCHANGE_BYTES=14, SNAPSHOT=15, INTENT=16, STATUS=17, COUNTERS=18,
         REQUEST_ID=19)
C = dict(CLAIM=1, RENEW=2, VALIDATE=3, COMMIT_CONFIG=4, STAGE_GENERATION=5,
         EXCHANGE_TX=6, CONTROL_INTENT=7, DISABLE=8, REVOKE=9, STATUS=10,
         COUNTERS=11, REMOVE_GATEWAY=12)
ST = dict(OWNED=1, STOPPING=2, OWNER_EPOCH=3, LEASE_MS=4, REVISION=5,
          STAGED=6, PEER=7)
PST = dict(SLOT=1, STATE=2, HAS_GEN=3, PMTU=4, ENDPOINT=5, PORT=6, INC=7)
STATE = dict(DOWN=0, READY=1, DISABLED=2, INVALID=3)
EPERM, ENOENT, EBUSY, ENODEV, EINVAL, ESTALE, EEXIST, EOPNOTSUPP, ERANGE = (
    1, 2, 16, 19, 22, 116, 17, 95, 34)

passed = failed = 0


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAIL {name} {detail}")


def attr(kind, payload, nested=False):
    kind |= NLA_F_NESTED if nested else 0
    raw = struct.pack("=HH", 4 + len(payload), kind) + payload
    return raw + b"\0" * (-len(raw) % 4)


def u16(v): return struct.pack("=H", v)
def u32(v): return struct.pack("=I", v)
def u64(v): return struct.pack("=Q", v)


def parse_attrs(data):
    out = {}
    while len(data) >= 4:
        length, kind = struct.unpack_from("=HH", data)
        if length < 4:
            break
        out.setdefault(kind & 0x3fff, []).append(data[4:length])
        data = data[(length + 3) & ~3:]
    return out


class Genl:
    def __init__(self):
        self.s = socket.socket(socket.AF_NETLINK, socket.SOCK_RAW, NETLINK_GENERIC)
        self.s.bind((0, 0))
        self.s.settimeout(5)
        self.portid = self.s.getsockname()[0]
        self.seq = 0
        self.family = GENL_ID_CTRL
        self.family = self.resolve()

    def send(self, family, cmd, attrs, version=1):
        self.seq += 1
        body = struct.pack("=BBH", cmd, version, 0) + b"".join(attrs)
        hdr = struct.pack("=IHHII", 16 + len(body), family,
                          NLM_F_REQUEST | NLM_F_ACK, self.seq, 0)
        self.s.send(hdr + body)

    def recv_all(self):
        """Returns (errno, reply attrs): errno 0 on ACK."""
        reply = {}
        while True:
            data = self.s.recv(65536)
            while len(data) >= 16:
                length, mtype, _, _, _ = struct.unpack_from("=IHHII", data)
                body = data[16:length]
                if mtype == NLMSG_ERROR:
                    return -struct.unpack_from("=i", body)[0], reply
                if mtype == self.family:
                    reply = parse_attrs(body[4:])
                data = data[(length + 3) & ~3:]

    def resolve(self):
        self.send(GENL_ID_CTRL, 3, [attr(2, b"vptunnel\0")], version=2)
        err, reply = self.recv_all()
        if err:
            raise RuntimeError(f"family vptunnel not found: {err}")
        return struct.unpack("=H", reply[1][0])[0]

    def cmd(self, name, *attrs):
        self.send(self.family, C[name], list(attrs))
        return self.recv_all()

    def close(self):
        self.s.close()


def a(name, value):
    return attr(A[name], value)


def owner(ifx, cid):
    return [a("IFINDEX", u32(ifx)), a("CONTROLLER_ID", cid)]


def pfx(addr, length):
    return socket.inet_aton(addr) + bytes([length])


UND = {"if": 3, "addr": "172.31.250.1"}  # the outer interface and address commit binds to


def snapshot(ifx, rules=(1, 2), key_peer1=0x20, endpoint1="172.31.250.12", und_addr=None):
    for raw in st.get(ST["PEER"], []):
        p = parse_attrs(raw)
        slot = struct.unpack("=H", p[PST["SLOT"]][0])[0]
        out["peers"][slot] = {"state": p[PST["STATE"]][0][0],
                              "gen": p[PST["HAS_GEN"]][0][0],
                              "inc": p[PST["INC"]][0]}
    return 0, out


def run_in_ns():
    os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWNET)
    os.system("ip link set lo up")
    if os.system("ip link add vpn0 type vpt1_ay1") != 0:
        sys.exit("cannot create vpn0 (is vpt1_foundation loaded?)")
    return socket.if_nametoindex("vpn0")


def main():
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        sys.exit("run as root in a disposable VM")
    ifx = run_in_ns()
    # Commit binds the outer UDP socket, so the snapshot's address must exist locally.
    os.system("ip link add dummy0 type dummy && ip addr add 172.31.250.1/24 dev dummy0 && ip link set dummy0 up")
    UND["if"] = socket.if_nametoindex("dummy0")
    ID1, ID2 = bytes(range(1, 17)), bytes(range(101, 117))
    g, g2 = Genl(), Genl()
    rid = a("REQUEST_ID", u64(0x1122334455667788))

    # Not claimed yet; wrong and unknown requests fail the whole request.
    check("status-before-claim", status(g, ifx)[0] == ENODEV)
    check("claim-wrong-ifindex", g.cmd("CLAIM", *owner(ifx + 50, ID1))[0] == ENODEV)
    check("claim-unknown-attribute",
          g.cmd("CLAIM", *owner(ifx, ID1), attr(20, b"\0\0\0\0"))[0] == EINVAL)
    check("claim-short-controller-id",
          g.cmd("CLAIM", a("IFINDEX", u32(ifx)), a("CONTROLLER_ID", b"x" * 8))[0] == ERANGE)
    check("claim-missing-controller-id", g.cmd("CLAIM", a("IFINDEX", u32(ifx)))[0] == EINVAL)
    check("claim-foreign-attribute",

def netns(name):

def attr(kind, payload, nested=False):
    kind |= NLA_F_NESTED if nested else 0
    raw = struct.pack("=HH", 4 + len(payload), kind) + payload
    return raw + b"\0" * (-len(raw) % 4)

        if length < 4:

        out.setdefault(kind & 0x3fff, []).append(data[4:length])
        data = data[(length + 3) & ~3:]
    return out


class Genl:
    def __init__(self):
        self.s = socket.socket(socket.AF_NETLINK, socket.SOCK_RAW, NETLINK_GENERIC)
        self.s.bind((0, 0))
        self.s.settimeout(5)
        self.portid = self.s.getsockname()[0]
        self.seq = 0
        self.family = GENL_ID_CTRL
        self.family = self.resolve()

    def send(self, family, cmd, attrs, version=1):
        self.seq += 1
        body = struct.pack("=BBH", cmd, version, 0) + b"".join(attrs)
        hdr = struct.pack("=IHHII", 16 + len(body), family,
                          NLM_F_REQUEST | NLM_F_ACK, self.seq, 0)
        self.s.send(hdr + body)

    def recv_all(self):
        """Returns (errno, reply attrs): errno 0 on ACK."""
        reply = {}
        while True:
            data = self.s.recv(65536)
            while len(data) >= 16:
                length, mtype, _, _, _ = struct.unpack_from("=IHHII", data)
                body = data[16:length]
                if mtype == NLMSG_ERROR:
                    return -struct.unpack_from("=i", body)[0], reply
                if mtype == self.family:
                    reply = parse_attrs(body[4:])
                data = data[(length + 3) & ~3:]

    def resolve(self):
        self.send(GENL_ID_CTRL, 3, [attr(2, b"vptunnel\0")], version=2)
        err, reply = self.recv_all()
        if err:
            raise RuntimeError(f"family vptunnel not found: {err}")
        return struct.unpack("=H", reply[1][0])[0]

    def cmd(self, name, *attrs):

        return self.recv_all()

    def close(self):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A configuration the controller accepts must be accepted by the kernel's VALIDATE.

Two implementations check the same rules: the controller's configuration loader and the kernel's
snapshot validation. A configuration the controller accepts but the kernel refuses would only show up
at run time as a controller that cannot start, so this test searches for one.

A seeded generator builds configurations that are valid by construction, then applies up to three
deliberate mutations (a boundary value, an overlap, a reserved range, a duplicate, a limit exceeded).
Every configuration goes through `vptctl snapshot`, which is the controller's own loader and snapshot
encoder, and every one it accepts is sent to the real kernel with VALIDATE. The property: the kernel
accepts all of them. Configurations the controller rejects are counted by reason, to show the generator
reaches the rules it is meant to probe.

Two controls keep the property from passing vacuously: a hand-made snapshot that breaks one kernel
rule must be refused (VALIDATE can say no), and the checked-in sample must be accepted by both.
A last, smaller part feeds corrupted snapshots to VALIDATE: any verdict is fine, a hang or a kernel
fault is not.

Run as root in a disposable VM with vpt1_foundation loaded:
    VPTCTL=/path/to/vptctl rj4_validate_corpus.py [--count N] [--seed S] [--keep DIR]
"""
import argparse
import collections
import ipaddress
import os
import random
import re
import socket
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import ay2_genl as G  # noqa: E402  (raw Generic Netlink helpers)

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
passed = failed = 0
LAN_IF, UND_IF = 11, 12  # interface indexes encoded into snapshots; VALIDATE only needs them nonzero


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAIL {name} {detail}")


# ---- Generator ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def net(rng, lo_len, hi_len, first_octets, avoid=()):
    """A random canonical IPv4 network not intersecting any of `avoid`, or None."""
    for _ in range(60):
        length = rng.randint(lo_len, hi_len)
        addr = rng.choice(first_octets) << 24 | rng.getrandbits(24)
        n = ipaddress.ip_network((addr, length), strict=False)
        if not any(n.overlaps(x) for x in avoid):
            return n
    return None


PUBLIC_FIRST = [o for o in range(1, 224) if o not in (10, 127, 169, 172, 192)]
LOCAL_POOLS = [[10], [192], [172]]


def host_in(rng, n, exclude=()):
    hosts = list(n.hosts()) if n.num_addresses <= 64 else None
    for _ in range(80):
        h = (hosts and rng.choice(hosts)) or ipaddress.ip_address(
            int(n.network_address) + rng.randint(1, n.num_addresses - 2))
        if h not in exclude and h != n.network_address and h != n.broadcast_address:
            return h
    return None


def sub(rng, parent, max_len=32):
    length = rng.randint(parent.prefixlen, max_len)
    off = rng.getrandbits(max(0, length - parent.prefixlen)) if length > parent.prefixlen else 0
    return ipaddress.ip_network(
        (int(parent.network_address) + (off << (32 - length)), length), strict=False)


def build(rng, keys, local_pub):
    """A configuration model that both implementations should accept."""
    lan = net(rng, 8, 28, rng.choice(LOCAL_POOLS))
    und = net(rng, 16, 28, [172, 198, 100], avoid=[lan])
    peers = []
    slots = rng.sample([1, 2, 3, 4], rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4]))
    taken = [lan, und]
    used_hosts = set()
    ends = set()
    own = host_in(rng, und)
    for i, slot in enumerate(sorted(slots, key=lambda _: rng.random())):
        prefixes = []
        for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, 4])):
            p = net(rng, 8, 32, PUBLIC_FIRST, avoid=taken)
            if p:
                prefixes.append(p)
                taken.append(p)
        if not prefixes:
            continue
        ep = host_in(rng, und, exclude={own} | ends)
        ends.add(ep)
        peers.append(dict(
            name=f"peer{i}", slot=slot, key=keys[i], endpoint=str(ep),
            role=rng.choice(["initiator", "responder"]),
            path_mtu=rng.choice([None, 1280, 1500, rng.randint(1280, 1500)]),
            prefixes=[str(p) for p in prefixes]))
    rules, ids = [], set()
    for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 12, 40, 128])):
        peer = rng.choice(peers)
        pfx = ipaddress.ip_network(rng.choice(peer["prefixes"]))
        local_side, peer_side = sub(rng, lan), sub(rng, pfx)
        outbound = rng.random() < 0.5
        proto = rng.choice(["tcp", "udp", "icmp-echo"])
        rid = rng.choice([rng.randint(1, 500), rng.randint(1, 2 ** 32 - 1)])
        while rid in ids:
            rid = rng.randint(1, 2 ** 32 - 1)
        ids.add(rid)
        rules.append(dict(
            id=rid, peer=peer["name"],
            source=str(local_side if outbound else peer_side),
            destination=str(peer_side if outbound else local_side),
            protocol=proto,
            ports=None if proto == "icmp-echo" else rng.choice(
                ["80", "22", "65535", "1", "1000-2000", "1-65535", "443-443"])))
    return dict(
        gw=dict(name="gw", lan_interface="lan0", underlay_interface="out0",
                lan_address=f"{host_in(rng, lan)}/{lan.prefixlen}",
                underlay_address=f"{own}/{und.prefixlen}"),
        peers=peers, rules=rules, lan=lan, und=und, local_pub=local_pub)


def mutations(rng, m, keys):
    """Each mutation moves one thing to or past a boundary. Most make the configuration invalid."""
    P = lambda: rng.choice(m["peers"])  # noqa: E731
    R = lambda: rng.choice(m["rules"]) if m["rules"] else None  # noqa: E731

    def mtu():
        P()["path_mtu"] = rng.choice([1279, 1281, 1499, 1501, 0, 65535, 1280, 1500])

    def prefix_reserved():
        P()["prefixes"].append(rng.choice(
            ["0.0.0.0/0", "0.0.0.0/8", "127.0.0.0/8", "127.1.2.0/24", "169.254.0.0/16", "224.0.0.0/4",
             "239.1.1.0/24", "240.0.0.0/4", "255.255.255.255/32", "1.2.3.4/32", "10.0.0.0/8"]))

    def prefix_overlap():
        p = P()
        p["prefixes"].append(str(rng.choice([m["lan"], m["und"],
                                             sub(rng, m["lan"]), sub(rng, m["und"]),
                                             ipaddress.ip_network(rng.choice(P()["prefixes"]))])))

    def prefix_noncanonical():
        p = P()
        n = ipaddress.ip_network(p["prefixes"][0])
        if n.prefixlen < 32:
            p["prefixes"][0] = f"{n.network_address + 1}/{n.prefixlen}"

    def prefix_count():
        p = P()
        p["prefixes"] = rng.choice([[], p["prefixes"] * 2, p["prefixes"][:1] * 5,
                                    p["prefixes"] + [f"{rng.randint(1, 120)}.9.9.0/24" for _ in range(4)]])

    def endpoint():
        p = P()
        p["endpoint"] = str(rng.choice([
            m["und"].network_address, m["und"].broadcast_address, m["gw"]["underlay_address"].split("/")[0],
            "8.8.8.8", "0.0.0.0", "255.255.255.255", "127.0.0.1",
            ipaddress.ip_network(P()["prefixes"][0]).network_address + 1,
            P()["endpoint"]]))

    def slot():
        P()["slot"] = rng.choice([0, 5, 255, P()["slot"]])

    def key():
        p = P()
        p["key"] = rng.choice([m["local_pub"], P()["key"], "00" * 32, "ff" * 32, "zz" * 32, "ab" * 31])

    def rule_count():
        extra = rng.choice([0, 128 - len(m["rules"]), 129 - len(m["rules"]), 200 - len(m["rules"])])
        if extra < 0:
            m["rules"] = m["rules"][:max(0, len(m["rules"]) + extra)]
            return
        r = m["rules"][0] if m["rules"] else None
        if r is None:
            return
        used = {x["id"] for x in m["rules"]}
        nxt = 1
        for _ in range(extra):
            while nxt in used:
                nxt += 1
            used.add(nxt)
            m["rules"].append(dict(r, id=nxt))
        if not extra:
            m["rules"] = []

    def rule_id():
        r = R()
        if r:
            r["id"] = rng.choice([0, 1, R()["id"], 2 ** 32 - 1, 2 ** 32, -1])

    def rule_shape():
        r = R()
        if r:
            r["peer"] = rng.choice(["nobody", "", r["peer"]])
            r["source"], r["destination"] = rng.choice([
                (r["source"], r["source"]), ("0.0.0.0/0", r["destination"]), (r["source"], "0.0.0.0/0"),
                (r["destination"], r["source"]), ("10.1.1.1/32", "10.1.1.2/32"),
                (r["source"], str(m["und"])), (r["source"], r["destination"])])

    def rule_ports():
        r = R()
        if r:
            r["protocol"] = rng.choice(["tcp", "udp", "icmp-echo", "sctp"])
            r["ports"] = rng.choice([None, "0", "65536", "0-0", "2000-1000", "1-65535", "80,443", "-1",
                                     "80", "1000-2000", "", "abc"])

    def lan():
        g = m["gw"]
        g["lan_address"] = rng.choice([f"{ipaddress.ip_address(g['lan_address'].split('/')[0])}/{n}"
                                       for n in (0, 8, 24, 30, 31, 32)])

    def underlay():
        g = m["gw"]
        g["underlay_address"] = rng.choice([f"{g['underlay_address'].split('/')[0]}/{n}" for n in (0, 16, 24, 31, 32)] +
                                           [g["lan_address"], "127.0.0.1/8", "0.0.0.0/0"])

    def ifnames():
        g = m["gw"]
        g[rng.choice(["lan_interface", "underlay_interface"])] = rng.choice(
            ["lo", "vpn0", ".", "..", "a" * 15, "a" * 16, "a b", "eth0/1", "", "out0", "lan0"])

    def names():
        p = P()
        p["name"] = rng.choice(["", "x" * 80, P()["name"], "has space", "ok-name_1.2"])

    return [mtu, prefix_reserved, prefix_overlap, prefix_noncanonical, prefix_count, endpoint, slot, key,
            rule_count, rule_id, rule_shape, rule_ports, lan, underlay, ifnames, names]


def render(m, key_file):
    def q(s):
        return '"' + str(s).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'

    g = m["gw"]
    out = ["[gateway]", f"name = {q(g['name'])}", f"private_key_file = {q(key_file)}",
           f"lan_interface = {q(g['lan_interface'])}", f"lan_address = {q(g['lan_address'])}",
           f"underlay_interface = {q(g['underlay_interface'])}",
           f"underlay_address = {q(g['underlay_address'])}", ""]
    for p in m["peers"]:
        out += ["[[peer]]", f"name = {q(p['name'])}", f"slot = {p['slot']}", f"public_key = {q(p['key'])}",
                f"endpoint = {q(p['endpoint'])}", f"role = {q(p['role'])}"]
        if p["path_mtu"] is not None:
            out.append(f"path_mtu = {p['path_mtu']}")
        out += ["prefixes = [" + ", ".join(q(x) for x in p["prefixes"]) + "]", ""]
    for r in m["rules"]:
        out += ["[[rule]]", f"id = {r['id']}", f"peer = {q(r['peer'])}", f"source = {q(r['source'])}",
                f"destination = {q(r['destination'])}", f"protocol = {q(r['protocol'])}"]
        if r["ports"] is not None:
            out.append(f"ports = {q(r['ports'])}")
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out)


# ---- Kernel side ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Kernel:
    def __init__(self):
        os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWNET)
        os.system("ip link set lo up")
        if os.system("ip link add vpn0 type vpt1_ay1") != 0:
            sys.exit("cannot create vpn0 (is vpt1_foundation loaded?)")
        self.ifx = socket.if_nametoindex("vpn0")
        self.cid = bytes(range(1, 17))
        self.g = G.Genl()
        err, _ = self.g.cmd("CLAIM", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid))
        if err:
            sys.exit(f"claim failed: {err}")
        self.last_renew = time.time()

    def validate(self, payload):
        if time.time() - self.last_renew > 1.0:  # the lease is 5 s
            self.g.cmd("RENEW", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid), G.a("CONFIG_REVISION", G.u64(0)))
            self.last_renew = time.time()
        return self.g.cmd("VALIDATE", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid), G.a("CONFIG_REVISION", G.u64(1)),
                          G.attr(G.A["SNAPSHOT"], payload, nested=True))[0]


def faults():
    out = subprocess.run("dmesg | grep -E 'BUG:|WARNING:|Oops|KASAN|UBSAN|refcount_t|lockdep' || true",
                         shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return out.strip()


# ---- Test ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def vptctl(vpt, *args):
    return subprocess.run([vpt, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)


def reason(stderr):
    """Group controller refusals by the field and the rule, not by the values."""
    line = stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1] if stderr.strip() else "?"
    line = re.sub(r"peer\.[^.:\s]*\.", "peer.N.", line)
    line = re.sub(r"rule\.\d+|\[\d+\]|\d+", "#", line)
    return line[:90]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("vptctl", nargs="?", default=os.environ.get("VPTCTL", ""))
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=1200)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261104)
    ap.add_argument("--keep", help="directory to keep every disagreement's configuration in")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        sys.exit("run as root in a disposable VM")
    if not args.vptctl or not os.path.exists(args.vptctl):
        sys.exit("set VPTCTL to the vptctl binary")
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rj4val_")
    os.chmod(tmp, 0o700)
    keydir = os.path.join(tmp, "keys")
    os.makedirs(keydir)
    pubs, local_key = [], os.path.join(keydir, "local.key")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A configuration the controller accepts must be accepted by the kernel's VALIDATE.

Two implementations check the same rules: the controller's configuration loader and the kernel's
snapshot validation. A configuration the controller accepts but the kernel refuses would only show up
at run time as a controller that cannot start, so this test searches for one.

A seeded generator builds configurations that are valid by construction, then applies up to three
deliberate mutations (a boundary value, an overlap, a reserved range, a duplicate, a limit exceeded).
Every configuration goes through `vptctl snapshot`, which is the controller's own loader and snapshot
encoder, and every one it accepts is sent to the real kernel with VALIDATE. The property: the kernel
accepts all of them. Configurations the controller rejects are counted by reason, to show the generator
reaches the rules it is meant to probe.

Two controls keep the property from passing vacuously: a hand-made snapshot that breaks one kernel
rule must be refused (VALIDATE can say no), and the checked-in sample must be accepted by both.
A last, smaller part feeds corrupted snapshots to VALIDATE: any verdict is fine, a hang or a kernel
fault is not.

Run as root in a disposable VM with vpt1_foundation loaded:
    VPTCTL=/path/to/vptctl rj4_validate_corpus.py [--count N] [--seed S] [--keep DIR]
"""
import argparse
import collections
import ipaddress
import os
import random
import re
import socket
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import ay2_genl as G  # noqa: E402  (raw Generic Netlink helpers)

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
passed = failed = 0
LAN_IF, UND_IF = 11, 12  # interface indexes encoded into snapshots; VALIDATE only needs them nonzero


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAIL {name} {detail}")


# ---- Generator ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def net(rng, lo_len, hi_len, first_octets, avoid=()):
    """A random canonical IPv4 network not intersecting any of `avoid`, or None."""
    for _ in range(60):
        length = rng.randint(lo_len, hi_len)
        addr = rng.choice(first_octets) << 24 | rng.getrandbits(24)
        n = ipaddress.ip_network((addr, length), strict=False)
        if not any(n.overlaps(x) for x in avoid):
            return n
    return None


PUBLIC_FIRST = [o for o in range(1, 224) if o not in (10, 127, 169, 172, 192)]
LOCAL_POOLS = [[10], [192], [172]]


def host_in(rng, n, exclude=()):
    hosts = list(n.hosts()) if n.num_addresses <= 64 else None
    for _ in range(80):
        h = (hosts and rng.choice(hosts)) or ipaddress.ip_address(
            int(n.network_address) + rng.randint(1, n.num_addresses - 2))
        if h not in exclude and h != n.network_address and h != n.broadcast_address:
            return h
    return None


def sub(rng, parent, max_len=32):
    length = rng.randint(parent.prefixlen, max_len)
    off = rng.getrandbits(max(0, length - parent.prefixlen)) if length > parent.prefixlen else 0
    return ipaddress.ip_network(
        (int(parent.network_address) + (off << (32 - length)), length), strict=False)


def build(rng, keys, local_pub):
    """A configuration model that both implementations should accept."""
    lan = net(rng, 8, 28, rng.choice(LOCAL_POOLS))
    und = net(rng, 16, 28, [172, 198, 100], avoid=[lan])
    peers = []
    slots = rng.sample([1, 2, 3, 4], rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4]))
    taken = [lan, und]
    used_hosts = set()
    ends = set()
    own = host_in(rng, und)
    for i, slot in enumerate(sorted(slots, key=lambda _: rng.random())):
        prefixes = []
        for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, 4])):
            p = net(rng, 8, 32, PUBLIC_FIRST, avoid=taken)
            if p:
                prefixes.append(p)
                taken.append(p)
        if not prefixes:
            continue
        ep = host_in(rng, und, exclude={own} | ends)
        ends.add(ep)
        peers.append(dict(
            name=f"peer{i}", slot=slot, key=keys[i], endpoint=str(ep),
            role=rng.choice(["initiator", "responder"]),
            path_mtu=rng.choice([None, 1280, 1500, rng.randint(1280, 1500)]),
            prefixes=[str(p) for p in prefixes]))
    rules, ids = [], set()
    for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 12, 40, 128])):
        peer = rng.choice(peers)
        pfx = ipaddress.ip_network(rng.choice(peer["prefixes"]))
        local_side, peer_side = sub(rng, lan), sub(rng, pfx)
        outbound = rng.random() < 0.5
        proto = rng.choice(["tcp", "udp", "icmp-echo"])
        rid = rng.choice([rng.randint(1, 500), rng.randint(1, 2 ** 32 - 1)])
        while rid in ids:
            rid = rng.randint(1, 2 ** 32 - 1)
        ids.add(rid)
        rules.append(dict(
            id=rid, peer=peer["name"],
            source=str(local_side if outbound else peer_side),
            destination=str(peer_side if outbound else local_side),
            protocol=proto,
            ports=None if proto == "icmp-echo" else rng.choice(
                ["80", "22", "65535", "1", "1000-2000", "1-65535", "443-443"])))

        gw=dict(name="gw", lan_interface="lan0", underlay_interface="out0",
                lan_address=f"{host_in(rng, lan)}/{lan.prefixlen}",
                underlay_address=f"{own}/{und.prefixlen}"),
        peers=peers, rules=rules, lan=lan, und=und, local_pub=local_pub)


def mutations(rng, m, keys):
    """Each mutation moves one thing to or past a boundary. Most make the configuration invalid."""
    P = lambda: rng.choice(m["peers"])  # noqa: E731
    R = lambda: rng.choice(m["rules"]) if m["rules"] else None  # noqa: E731

        P()["path_mtu"] = rng.choice([1279, 1281, 1499, 1501, 0, 65535, 1280, 1500])

    def prefix_reserved():

             "239.1.1.0/24", "240.0.0.0/4", "255.255.255.255/32", "1.2.3.4/32", "10.0.0.0/8"]))

        p = P()

                                             sub(rng, m["lan"]), sub(rng, m["und"]),
                                             ipaddress.ip_network(rng.choice(P()["prefixes"]))])))

    def prefix_noncanonical():
        p = P()
        n = ipaddress.ip_network(p["prefixes"][0])
        if n.prefixlen < 32:
            p["prefixes"][0] = f"{n.network_address + 1}/{n.prefixlen}"

    def prefix_count():
        p = P()
        p["prefixes"] = rng.choice([[], p["prefixes"] * 2, p["prefixes"][:1] * 5,
                                    p["prefixes"] + [f"{rng.randint(1, 120)}.9.9.0/24" for _ in range(4)]])

    def endpoint():
        p = P()
        p["endpoint"] = str(rng.choice([
            m["und"].network_address, m["und"].broadcast_address, m["gw"]["underlay_address"].split("/")[0],
            "8.8.8.8", "0.0.0.0", "255.255.255.255", "127.0.0.1",
            ipaddress.ip_network(P()["prefixes"][0]).network_address + 1,
            P()["endpoint"]]))

    def slot():
        P()["slot"] = rng.choice([0, 5, 255, P()["slot"]])

    def key():
        p = P()
        p["key"] = rng.choice([m["local_pub"], P()["key"], "00" * 32, "ff" * 32, "zz" * 32, "ab" * 31])

    def rule_count():
        extra = rng.choice([0, 128 - len(m["rules"]), 129 - len(m["rules"]), 200 - len(m["rules"])])
        if extra < 0:
            m["rules"] = m["rules"][:max(0, len(m["rules"]) + extra)]
            return
        r = m["rules"][0] if m["rules"] else None
        if r is None:
            return
        used = {x["id"] for x in m["rules"]}
        nxt = 1
        for _ in range(extra):
            while nxt in used:
                nxt += 1
            used.add(nxt)
            m["rules"].append(dict(r, id=nxt))
        if not extra:
            m["rules"] = []

        r = R()
        if r:
            r["id"] = rng.choice([0, 1, R()["id"], 2 ** 32 - 1, 2 ** 32, -1])

    def rule_shape():
        r = R()
        if r:
            r["peer"] = rng.choice(["nobody", "", r["peer"]])
            r["source"], r["destination"] = rng.choice([
                (r["source"], r["source"]), ("0.0.0.0/0", r["destination"]), (r["source"], "0.0.0.0/0"),
                (r["destination"], r["source"]), ("10.1.1.1/32", "10.1.1.2/32"),
                (r["source"], str(m["und"])), (r["source"], r["destination"])])

    def rule_ports():
        r = R()
        if r:
            r["protocol"] = rng.choice(["tcp", "udp", "icmp-echo", "sctp"])
            r["ports"] = rng.choice([None, "0", "65536", "0-0", "2000-1000", "1-65535", "80,443", "-1",
                                     "80", "1000-2000", "", "abc"])

    def lan():
        g = m["gw"]
        g["lan_address"] = rng.choice([f"{ipaddress.ip_address(g['lan_address'].split('/')[0])}/{n}"
                                       for n in (0, 8, 24, 30, 31, 32)])

    def underlay():
        g = m["gw"]
        g["underlay_address"] = rng.choice([f"{g['underlay_address'].split('/')[0]}/{n}" for n in (0, 16, 24, 31, 32)] +
                                           [g["lan_address"], "127.0.0.1/8", "0.0.0.0/0"])

    def ifnames():
        g = m["gw"]
        g[rng.choice(["lan_interface", "underlay_interface"])] = rng.choice(
            ["lo", "vpn0", ".", "..", "a" * 15, "a" * 16, "a b", "eth0/1", "", "out0", "lan0"])

    def names():
        p = P()
        p["name"] = rng.choice(["", "x" * 80, P()["name"], "has space", "ok-name_1.2"])

    return [mtu, prefix_reserved, prefix_overlap, prefix_noncanonical, prefix_count, endpoint, slot, key,
            rule_count, rule_id, rule_shape, rule_ports, lan, underlay, ifnames, names]


def render(m, key_file):
    def q(s):
        return '"' + str(s).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'

    g = m["gw"]
    out = ["[gateway]", f"name = {q(g['name'])}", f"private_key_file = {q(key_file)}",
           f"lan_interface = {q(g['lan_interface'])}", f"lan_address = {q(g['lan_address'])}",
           f"underlay_interface = {q(g['underlay_interface'])}",
           f"underlay_address = {q(g['underlay_address'])}", ""]
    for p in m["peers"]:
        out += ["[[peer]]", f"name = {q(p['name'])}", f"slot = {p['slot']}", f"public_key = {q(p['key'])}",
                f"endpoint = {q(p['endpoint'])}", f"role = {q(p['role'])}"]
        if p["path_mtu"] is not None:
            out.append(f"path_mtu = {p['path_mtu']}")
        out += ["prefixes = [" + ", ".join(q(x) for x in p["prefixes"]) + "]", ""]
    for r in m["rules"]:
        out += ["[[rule]]", f"id = {r['id']}", f"peer = {q(r['peer'])}", f"source = {q(r['source'])}",
                f"destination = {q(r['destination'])}", f"protocol = {q(r['protocol'])}"]
        if r["ports"] is not None:
            out.append(f"ports = {q(r['ports'])}")
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out)


# ---- Kernel side ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Kernel:
    def __init__(self):
        os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWNET)
        os.system("ip link set lo up")
        if os.system("ip link add vpn0 type vpt1_ay1") != 0:
            sys.exit("cannot create vpn0 (is vpt1_foundation loaded?)")
        self.ifx = socket.if_nametoindex("vpn0")

        self.g = G.Genl()
        err, _ = self.g.cmd("CLAIM", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid))
        if err:
            sys.exit(f"claim failed: {err}")
        self.last_renew = time.time()

    def validate(self, payload):
        if time.time() - self.last_renew > 1.0:  # the lease is 5 s
            self.g.cmd("RENEW", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid), G.a("CONFIG_REVISION", G.u64(0)))
            self.last_renew = time.time()
        return self.g.cmd("VALIDATE", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid), G.a("CONFIG_REVISION", G.u64(1)),
                          G.attr(G.A["SNAPSHOT"], payload, nested=True))[0]


def faults():
    out = subprocess.run("dmesg | grep -E 'BUG:|WARNING:|Oops|KASAN|UBSAN|refcount_t|lockdep' || true",
                         shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

# ---- Test ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def vptctl(vpt, *args):
    return subprocess.run([vpt, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)

    """Group controller refusals by the field and the rule, not by the values."""
    line = stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1] if stderr.strip() else "?"

    check("sample-is-accepted-by-the-controller", r.returncode == 0, r.stderr[-200:])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A configuration the controller accepts must be accepted by the kernel's VALIDATE.

Two implementations check the same rules: the controller's configuration loader and the kernel's
snapshot validation. A configuration the controller accepts but the kernel refuses would only show up
at run time as a controller that cannot start, so this test searches for one.

A seeded generator builds configurations that are valid by construction, then applies up to three
deliberate mutations (a boundary value, an overlap, a reserved range, a duplicate, a limit exceeded).
Every configuration goes through `vptctl snapshot`, which is the controller's own loader and snapshot
encoder, and every one it accepts is sent to the real kernel with VALIDATE. The property: the kernel
accepts all of them. Configurations the controller rejects are counted by reason, to show the generator
reaches the rules it is meant to probe.

Two controls keep the property from passing vacuously: a hand-made snapshot that breaks one kernel
rule must be refused (VALIDATE can say no), and the checked-in sample must be accepted by both.
A last, smaller part feeds corrupted snapshots to VALIDATE: any verdict is fine, a hang or a kernel
fault is not.

Run as root in a disposable VM with vpt1_foundation loaded:
    VPTCTL=/path/to/vptctl rj4_validate_corpus.py [--count N] [--seed S] [--keep DIR]
"""
import argparse
import collections
import ipaddress
import os
import random
import re
import socket
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import ay2_genl as G  # noqa: E402  (raw Generic Netlink helpers)

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
passed = failed = 0
LAN_IF, UND_IF = 11, 12  # interface indexes encoded into snapshots; VALIDATE only needs them nonzero


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAIL {name} {detail}")


# ---- Generator ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def net(rng, lo_len, hi_len, first_octets, avoid=()):
    """A random canonical IPv4 network not intersecting any of `avoid`, or None."""
    for _ in range(60):
        length = rng.randint(lo_len, hi_len)
        addr = rng.choice(first_octets) << 24 | rng.getrandbits(24)
        n = ipaddress.ip_network((addr, length), strict=False)
        if not any(n.overlaps(x) for x in avoid):
            return n
    return None


PUBLIC_FIRST = [o for o in range(1, 224) if o not in (10, 127, 169, 172, 192)]
LOCAL_POOLS = [[10], [192], [172]]


def host_in(rng, n, exclude=()):
    hosts = list(n.hosts()) if n.num_addresses <= 64 else None
    for _ in range(80):
        h = (hosts and rng.choice(hosts)) or ipaddress.ip_address(
            int(n.network_address) + rng.randint(1, n.num_addresses - 2))
        if h not in exclude and h != n.network_address and h != n.broadcast_address:
            return h
    return None


def sub(rng, parent, max_len=32):
    length = rng.randint(parent.prefixlen, max_len)
    off = rng.getrandbits(max(0, length - parent.prefixlen)) if length > parent.prefixlen else 0
    return ipaddress.ip_network(
        (int(parent.network_address) + (off << (32 - length)), length), strict=False)


def build(rng, keys, local_pub):
    """A configuration model that both implementations should accept."""
    lan = net(rng, 8, 28, rng.choice(LOCAL_POOLS))
    und = net(rng, 16, 28, [172, 198, 100], avoid=[lan])
    peers = []
    slots = rng.sample([1, 2, 3, 4], rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4]))
    taken = [lan, und]
    used_hosts = set()
    ends = set()
    own = host_in(rng, und)
    for i, slot in enumerate(sorted(slots, key=lambda _: rng.random())):
        prefixes = []
        for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, 4])):
            p = net(rng, 8, 32, PUBLIC_FIRST, avoid=taken)
            if p:
                prefixes.append(p)
                taken.append(p)
        if not prefixes:

        ends.add(ep)
        peers.append(dict(
            name=f"peer{i}", slot=slot, key=keys[i], endpoint=str(ep),
            role=rng.choice(["initiator", "responder"]),
            path_mtu=rng.choice([None, 1280, 1500, rng.randint(1280, 1500)]),
            prefixes=[str(p) for p in prefixes]))
    rules, ids = [], set()
    for _ in range(rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 12, 40, 128])):
        peer = rng.choice(peers)
        pfx = ipaddress.ip_network(rng.choice(peer["prefixes"]))
        local_side, peer_side = sub(rng, lan), sub(rng, pfx)
        outbound = rng.random() < 0.5
        proto = rng.choice(["tcp", "udp", "icmp-echo"])
        rid = rng.choice([rng.randint(1, 500), rng.randint(1, 2 ** 32 - 1)])
        while rid in ids:
            rid = rng.randint(1, 2 ** 32 - 1)
        ids.add(rid)
        rules.append(dict(
            id=rid, peer=peer["name"],
            source=str(local_side if outbound else peer_side),
            destination=str(peer_side if outbound else local_side),
            protocol=proto,
            ports=None if proto == "icmp-echo" else rng.choice(
                ["80", "22", "65535", "1", "1000-2000", "1-65535", "443-443"])))
    return dict(
        gw=dict(name="gw", lan_interface="lan0", underlay_interface="out0",
                lan_address=f"{host_in(rng, lan)}/{lan.prefixlen}",
                underlay_address=f"{own}/{und.prefixlen}"),
        peers=peers, rules=rules, lan=lan, und=und, local_pub=local_pub)


def mutations(rng, m, keys):
    """Each mutation moves one thing to or past a boundary. Most make the configuration invalid."""
    P = lambda: rng.choice(m["peers"])  # noqa: E731
    R = lambda: rng.choice(m["rules"]) if m["rules"] else None  # noqa: E731

    def mtu():
        P()["path_mtu"] = rng.choice([1279, 1281, 1499, 1501, 0, 65535, 1280, 1500])

    def prefix_reserved():

            ["0.0.0.0/0", "0.0.0.0/8", "127.0.0.0/8", "127.1.2.0/24", "169.254.0.0/16", "224.0.0.0/4",
             "239.1.1.0/24", "240.0.0.0/4", "255.255.255.255/32", "1.2.3.4/32", "10.0.0.0/8"]))

        p = P()

                                             sub(rng, m["lan"]), sub(rng, m["und"]),
                                             ipaddress.ip_network(rng.choice(P()["prefixes"]))])))

    def prefix_noncanonical():
        p = P()
        n = ipaddress.ip_network(p["prefixes"][0])
        if n.prefixlen < 32:
            p["prefixes"][0] = f"{n.network_address + 1}/{n.prefixlen}"

    def prefix_count():
        p = P()
        p["prefixes"] = rng.choice([[], p["prefixes"] * 2, p["prefixes"][:1] * 5,
                                    p["prefixes"] + [f"{rng.randint(1, 120)}.9.9.0/24" for _ in range(4)]])

    def endpoint():
        p = P()
        p["endpoint"] = str(rng.choice([
            m["und"].network_address, m["und"].broadcast_address, m["gw"]["underlay_address"].split("/")[0],
            "8.8.8.8", "0.0.0.0", "255.255.255.255", "127.0.0.1",
            ipaddress.ip_network(P()["prefixes"][0]).network_address + 1,
            P()["endpoint"]]))

    def slot():
        P()["slot"] = rng.choice([0, 5, 255, P()["slot"]])

    def key():
        p = P()
        p["key"] = rng.choice([m["local_pub"], P()["key"], "00" * 32, "ff" * 32, "zz" * 32, "ab" * 31])

    def rule_count():
        extra = rng.choice([0, 128 - len(m["rules"]), 129 - len(m["rules"]), 200 - len(m["rules"])])
        if extra < 0:

    def rule_shape():
        r = R()
        if r:
            r["peer"] = rng.choice(["nobody", "", r["peer"]])
            r["source"], r["destination"] = rng.choice([
                (r["source"], r["source"]), ("0.0.0.0/0", r["destination"]), (r["source"], "0.0.0.0/0"),
                (r["destination"], r["source"]), ("10.1.1.1/32", "10.1.1.2/32"),
                (r["source"], str(m["und"])), (r["source"], r["destination"])])

    def rule_ports():
        r = R()
        if r:
            r["protocol"] = rng.choice(["tcp", "udp", "icmp-echo", "sctp"])
            r["ports"] = rng.choice([None, "0", "65536", "0-0", "2000-1000", "1-65535", "80,443", "-1",
                                     "80", "1000-2000", "", "abc"])

    def lan():

                                       for n in (0, 8, 24, 30, 31, 32)])

                                           [g["lan_address"], "127.0.0.1/8", "0.0.0.0/0"])

    def ifnames():
        g = m["gw"]
        g[rng.choice(["lan_interface", "underlay_interface"])] = rng.choice(
            ["lo", "vpn0", ".", "..", "a" * 15, "a" * 16, "a b", "eth0/1", "", "out0", "lan0"])

    def names():
        p = P()
        p["name"] = rng.choice(["", "x" * 80, P()["name"], "has space", "ok-name_1.2"])

    return [mtu, prefix_reserved, prefix_overlap, prefix_noncanonical, prefix_count, endpoint, slot, key,
            rule_count, rule_id, rule_shape, rule_ports, lan, underlay, ifnames, names]


def render(m, key_file):
    def q(s):
        return '"' + str(s).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'

    g = m["gw"]
    out = ["[gateway]", f"name = {q(g['name'])}", f"private_key_file = {q(key_file)}",
           f"lan_interface = {q(g['lan_interface'])}", f"lan_address = {q(g['lan_address'])}",
           f"underlay_interface = {q(g['underlay_interface'])}",
           f"underlay_address = {q(g['underlay_address'])}", ""]
    for p in m["peers"]:
        out += ["[[peer]]", f"name = {q(p['name'])}", f"slot = {p['slot']}", f"public_key = {q(p['key'])}",
                f"endpoint = {q(p['endpoint'])}", f"role = {q(p['role'])}"]
        if p["path_mtu"] is not None:
            out.append(f"path_mtu = {p['path_mtu']}")
        out += ["prefixes = [" + ", ".join(q(x) for x in p["prefixes"]) + "]", ""]
    for r in m["rules"]:
        out += ["[[rule]]", f"id = {r['id']}", f"peer = {q(r['peer'])}", f"source = {q(r['source'])}",
                f"destination = {q(r['destination'])}", f"protocol = {q(r['protocol'])}"]
        if r["ports"] is not None:
            out.append(f"ports = {q(r['ports'])}")
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out)


# ---- Kernel side ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Kernel:
    def __init__(self):
        os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWNET)
        os.system("ip link set lo up")
        if os.system("ip link add vpn0 type vpt1_ay1") != 0:
            sys.exit("cannot create vpn0 (is vpt1_foundation loaded?)")
        self.ifx = socket.if_nametoindex("vpn0")
        self.cid = bytes(range(1, 17))
        self.g = G.Genl()
        err, _ = self.g.cmd("CLAIM", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid))
        if err:
            sys.exit(f"claim failed: {err}")
        self.last_renew = time.time()

    def validate(self, payload):
        if time.time() - self.last_renew > 1.0:  # the lease is 5 s
            self.g.cmd("RENEW", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid), G.a("CONFIG_REVISION", G.u64(0)))
            self.last_renew = time.time()
        return self.g.cmd("VALIDATE", *G.owner(self.ifx, self.cid), G.a("CONFIG_REVISION", G.u64(1)),
                          G.attr(G.A["SNAPSHOT"], payload, nested=True))[0]


def faults():
    out = subprocess.run("dmesg | grep -E 'BUG:|WARNING:|Oops|KASAN|UBSAN|refcount_t|lockdep' || true",
                         shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return out.strip()

def vptctl(vpt, *args):
    return subprocess.run([vpt, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)


def reason(stderr):
    """Group controller refusals by the field and the rule, not by the values."""
    line = stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1] if stderr.strip() else "?"
    line = re.sub(r"peer\.[^.:\s]*\.", "peer.N.", line)
    line = re.sub(r"rule\.\d+|\[\d+\]|\d+", "#", line)
    return line[:90]


def main():

Check the controller's configuration rules against the kernel's VALIDATE; refuse an empty rule set

The controller and the kernel each validate a configuration. A configuration the
controller accepts but the kernel refuses would only appear at run time, as a
controller that cannot start. tests/netns/rj4_validate_corpus.py searches for one: a
seeded generator builds 1,200 to 1,500 configurations (valid by construction, then up
to three boundary mutations), each goes through the controller's own loader and
snapshot encoder, and every accepted one is sent to the real kernel's VALIDATE.

It found one: a configuration with no rules was accepted by the controller and refused
by the kernel with -EINVAL. The controller then retried every 2 s forever. The loader
now requires at least one rule.

- vptctl snapshot CONFIG --lan-ifindex N --underlay-ifindex M prints the SNAPSHOT payload
  (hex) that vptctl run would send; it validates the configuration and key first.
- control/tests/snapshot_cli.rs: the printed bytes equal encode_snapshot's, and it
  refuses a missing file, an invalid configuration and a missing key.
- Added to tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh. Controls: a forged path MTU of 1279 is refused by
  the kernel, the sample configuration is accepted by both; 400 corrupted snapshots
  must be judged without a hang or a kernel fault.
EOF

cd "/Users/rajmodi/Documents/5th sem/CN/VPNTunnel/.claude/worktrees/testing-strategy-linux-12bffd" && gh pr create --repo Aayush75/VPNTunnel --base main --head raj/validate-differential --title "Check the controller's configuration rules against the kernel's VALIDATE; refuse an empty rule set" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why
In the #45 review I said I would replace the deleted `control/tests/perimeter.rs` cross-check with a permanent one. The controller's configuration loader and the kernel's snapshot validation are two implementations of the same rules. A configuration the controller accepts but the kernel refuses would only show up at run time, as a controller that cannot start.

## A bug it found
A configuration with **no `[[rule]]` sections** was accepted by the controller and refused by the kernel (`VALIDATE` returns `-EINVAL`: `vpt1_gw_validate` rejects `!s->rule_count`). `vptctl run` on such a file would claim the gateway, fail at `VALIDATE`, and retry every 2 s forever. The controller loader now requires at least one rule (`config.rs`, with a unit test; `control/README.md` says `1..=128`). The #43 contract and my earlier one-off comparison (which compared only the kernel's domain/rule checks, not whole snapshots) did not catch this.

## Behavior added
- `vptctl snapshot CONFIG --lan-ifindex N --underlay-ifindex M` prints the SNAPSHOT payload (hex) that `vptctl run` would send. It loads and validates the configuration and the gateway key first, talks to no kernel, and uses the same `encode_snapshot` as the daemon. `control/tests/snapshot_cli.rs`: the printed bytes equal `encode_snapshot`'s, and it refuses a missing file, an invalid configuration and a missing key.
- `tests/netns/rj4_validate_corpus.py` (added to `tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh`): a seeded generator builds configurations that are valid by construction, then applies up to three boundary mutations (path MTU 1279..1501, reserved/overlapping/non-canonical prefixes, duplicate or out-of-range slots, keys and endpoints, 0..200 rules, port ranges, interface names). Every configuration goes through `vptctl snapshot`; every one it accepts is sent to the real kernel's `VALIDATE`, which must accept it. Controls: a snapshot forged to break one kernel rule (path MTU 1279) is refused, and the sample is accepted by both; 400 corrupted snapshots must be judged without a hang or a kernel fault. The controller's own refusals are counted by reason (about 65 kinds), so the generator is shown to reach the rules it is meant to probe. It tests only the direction that matters (controller accepts, kernel refuses); the controller being stricter is intended.

No wire, Netlink or kernel change.

## Tests and environment
- AN1 reference VM `6.18.0-vpt1-ref` (x86-64, QEMU TCG on an Apple Silicon Mac), release controller and module built in the guest. After the fix, three seeds of 1,500 configurations: 569, 563 and 587 accepted by the controller, **0 disagreements**; the default run (1,200) 445 accepted, 0 disagreements, no kernel fault markers. Before the fix the same seed gave 6 disagreements, all zero-rule configurations.
- Mutation checks: relaxing the controller's path-MTU minimum to 1000 gives 2 disagreements; raising its rule limit from 128 to 130 gives 12 (kernel `-E2BIG`). Both fail the test; both were restored and rebuilt before the final run.
- macOS: fmt, locked Clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --locked` (97 library tests plus the integration tests), doc links.
- **Not run:** the rest of `tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh` on this head, ARM64/Pi, debug-kernel configs. The corpus is bounded and seeded: a pass is 0 disagreements in these draws, not a proof.

## Overlap
`tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh` and `docs/CONTROLLER.md` are also touched by #54; the hunks are adjacent additions, expect a trivial rebase for whichever merges second.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
PR [#55](https://github.com/Aayush75/VPNTunnel/pull/55) is open for item 4, authored only as rajmodi8905 with no Claude trailers. The new test found a real bug.

**The bug:** a config with no `[[rule]]` sections passed the controller's loader but was refused by the kernel with `-EINVAL`. A controller started on it would have retried every 2 s forever. The controller now requires at least one rule. My old one-off comparison missed this because it compared only the kernel's domain and rule checks, not whole snapshots.

**What the PR adds:**
- **`vptctl snapshot`:** a new command that prints the exact snapshot bytes `vptctl run` would send, without talking to a kernel. Two portable tests cover it.
- **`tests/netns/rj4_validate_corpus.py`:**
  - **Generator:** builds 1,200–1,500 configs, valid by construction, then applies up to three boundary mutations.
  - **Property checked:** every config the controller accepts goes to the real kernel's `VALIDATE`, which must accept it.
  - **Controls:** a forged path MTU of 1279 is refused, the sample config is accepted by both, and 400 corrupted snapshots must not hang or fault the kernel.
  - **Suite:** the test is added to the kernel VM suite.

**Verified on the reference VM:**
- **Before the fix:** the same seed gave 6 disagreements, all zero-rule configs.
- **After the fix:** three seeds of 1,500 configs gave 569, 563 and 587 accepted, with 0 disagreements. The default 1,200-config run gave 445 accepted, 0 disagreements and no kernel fault markers.
- **Mutation checks:**
  - **Path-MTU minimum:** relaxing it to 1000 gives 2 disagreements.
  - **Rule limit:** raising it from 128 to 130 gives 12.
  - **Final run:** both were restored and rebuilt before it.
- **macOS:** the format check, Clippy and all tests pass.

**Limits:**
- **Not run:** the rest of the kernel suite on this head, and ARM64 or the Pi.
- **Not a proof:** the corpus is seeded and bounded, so a pass means 0 disagreements in these draws.
- **Merge conflicts:** the PR touches `kernel_vm_suite.sh` and `docs/CONTROLLER.md`, as #54 does. Expect a trivial rebase for whichever merges second.

The reference VM is stopped. Your open PRs are now #51, #52, #53, #54 and #55. Nobody has reviewed #51 or #52, and I haven't read their diffs myself. Should I read both now?

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - VPT1 controller (`vptctl run`): one session per claim. Netlink flow: claim → VALIDATE → COMMIT_CONFIG → STATUS. Lease renewed every 1 s (5 s lease). Re-key after 90 s. INIT retry/backoff. Session-level errors retry every 2 s.
   - Kernel COMMIT_CONFIG semantics (gateway.c `vpt1_gw_commit`):
     - A later revision N+1 keeps a peer only if `peer_cfg_equal` holds (role, pmtu, endpoint, key, prefixes, slot).
     - Otherwise the peer is replaced with a new incarnation.
     - A global change (`global_equal`: ifindexes, underlay address, local key, LAN/underlay prefixes) replaces all peers and rebinds.
   - Controller follows STATUS incarnations rather than repeating the kernel's classification.
   - Both gateways enforce policy (sender and receiver), so a rule opens a port only when both have it.
   - Kernel VALIDATE (`snapshot_check`): needs a nonzero rule_count, pmtu 1280..1500, 1..4 prefixes per peer, distinct keys/endpoints, a local key different from peer keys, and at most 128 rules (129 → -E2BIG/EINVAL).
   - `-ENOSPC`/`-EBUSY` are failed transactions (#43 contract). Rounded allocation charge: cfg 1024 B bucket + ACL bucket (1280 B for two rules, 5120 B for 128).

   - Mutation checks and seeded differential/corpus testing.

       ```
       for ifname in "${LAN_IF}" "${UNDERLAY_IF}"; do
           ip link show "${ifname}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vpt-gateway: no interface ${ifname} (check lan_interface and underlay_interface in ${CONFIG}; \`ip -br link\` lists the real names)" >&2; exit 2; }
       done

       - Otherwise the peer is rebuilt `Idle{not_before: now}` with no cache.
       - Slots no longer in the config are removed.

content.content:
=== #61
Makes two points of TECHNICAL_DESIGN section 5 true that were only convention before: the **kernel** chooses each attempt's ID and each receive locator, and `STAGE_GENERATION` cannot use ones it did not issue. Full description and the list of what is *not* done: `docs/AY4_ATTEMPTS.md`.

**This is an ABI addition, so I'm asking Raj to agree before it merges** (one new command, `BEGIN_ATTEMPT = 13`; the controller and the Netlink conformance tests change with it).

- `BEGIN_ATTEMPT`: kernel picks a random attempt ID (initiator) and a collision-checked, nonzero receive locator; one pending attempt per peer, valid 10 s.
- `STAGE_GENERATION`: only for that attempt, with that locator, once. `EXCHANGE_TX`: only the pending attempt's own INIT/RESPONSE.
- Responder: may only begin the attempt of the last INIT the kernel delivered for that peer (so the controller cannot invent one).
- A completed attempt can still send for 20 s, so the responder can answer duplicate INITs from its cache.
- Controller: asks the kernel through a new `Port::begin_attempt` instead of drawing random values.

**Run on the 6.18 reference VM** (long-lived working copy, not the AN1 master): gateway unit test 1092 assertions (440 new); `ay2_genl` and `ay2_datapath` now go through `BEGIN_ATTEMPT`; `ay2_controller`, `ay4_usage_rekey`, `ay4_silence`, `ay4_soak`, `ay5_runtime`, `demo_reachability` pass in debug and release with a controller built from this branch; `hr4_ip` passes (196 cases) after I updated it to use the issued locators. Sparse, clang, checkpatch unchanged; clippy `-D warnings` clean, 103 controller unit tests.

One honest note: my first full run failed every controller test because the responder consumed the attempt when it installed keys and then could not send its RESPONSE. I fixed that (the attempt stays valid for sending, not for staging) and re-ran; the numbers above are from the fixed code. The last full-suite run was before I changed `hr4_ip.py`; I re-ran `hr4_ip` and `ay2_datapath` on their own afterwards, not the whole suite again.

**Not in this PR** (design section 5): the encrypted CONFIRM / READY / COMMIT / COMMITTED activation, granted rekey (`REKEY_START` / `REKEY_OK`, mode 1), kernel PING/PONG liveness, and an acknowledging reply to a duplicate `STAGE_GENERATION`.
=== #63
**Stacked on #61** (kernel-issued attempts): the base is that branch, and the tests key the gateways through `BEGIN_ATTEMPT`. Review #61 first; this diff is only the liveness change. When #61 merges the base moves to `main`.

Puts TECHNICAL_DESIGN section 8 in the kernel (subtypes 6 and 7 were already in the wire spec and the parser). Details, differences from the design and the full evidence: `docs/AY4_LIVENESS.md`. No change to the wire format of anything that exists, to the controller, or to existing Netlink IDs (six counters are appended).

- PING every 5 s per relationship from the gateway worker; every authenticated PING under the **current** generation is answered with a PONG. A PING under a next or retiring generation is dropped and counted.
- A round trip is a PONG that echoes one of at most three live challenges, once. Inbound data, inbound PINGs and repeats do not refresh health, so a one-way failure is not hidden.
- 15 s with no round trip closes the peer: admission fails both ways, PINGs stop, its continuity ends (once, counted as `LIVENESS_LOST`). A late PONG does not reopen it; a generation installed over a closed peer is treated as a new session (old keys dropped, new continuity), which is how a re-keying controller recovers it.
- A lapsed lease silences both PINGs and answers.

**Behaviour change to be aware of:** a stage over a still-valid current generation was always a rekey; on a *closed* peer it is now a fresh session.

**Run on the 6.18 reference VM** (long-lived working copy, not the AN1 master): full `kernel_vm_suite.sh` with a controller built from the #61 branch, debug and release, `KERNEL_VM_SUITE PASS` (gateway test 1136 assertions; the existing controller, usage re-key, silence, soak, runtime and demo tests all still pass with PINGs on every tunnel). New: `liveness` and `liveness_loss` unit tests (the second really waits 17 s) and `tests/netns/ay4_liveness.py` (36 checks, no controller process: PING/PONG on an idle tunnel; a one-way failure closes both sides at about 15 s while B is still receiving A's traffic, counted once; closed means no traffic and no PINGs; the underlay returning does not reopen it; a new session does). Sparse, clang and checkpatch unchanged. Mutations caught: closure never happening, a late PONG reopening, a PING never answered, a new generation on a closed peer treated as a rekey, a PONG that does not consume its challenge.

- Controller: asks the kernel through a new `Port::begin_attempt` instead of drawing random values.

3. `docs/CONTROLLER.md` and `tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh` also conflict with #52 and #55 (adjacent additions only).

Not run: the rest of the suite on this head alone, a multi-peer reload on the VM (removal of one of several peers is unit-tested only), ARM64, a Pi. I am not approving; merging is for Aayush to decide.

Clarification of item 2 in my review above, which was worded badly. After #51 merges, `daemon.rs` takes every time value from `BootClock` (`clock.now()`). This PR's new `reload()` calls `Instant::now()` itself when it hands the time to `Controller::reconfigure()`, and its loop still uses `Instant::now()`. Whichever PR merges second has to switch those to `clock.now()`: pass the time into `reload()` as a parameter. I did exactly that in my test merge, and it built and passed.

**The bug is real.** `vpt1_gw_validate` rejects a snapshot with `!s->rule_count` (`gateway.c:934`), so a configuration with no rules was accepted by the controller and refused by the kernel, leaving a controller that claims, fails `VALIDATE` and retries every 2 s forever. 1. The corpus only tests the direction that matters (controller accepts, kernel refuses), as you say. It will not notice the controller being stricter than needed, so a rule that is wrongly refused would only show up as a user complaint. A small fixed list of configurations that must be accepted would cover that cheaply.
2. A pass is "0 disagreements in these draws" and you say so. Running the other two seeds you mention in the suite as well would cost little.
3. `vptctl snapshot` needs the private key file present, which is fine, but say so in `--help` since it is surprising for a command that "talks to no kernel".
4. Overlap with #54 in `kernel_vm_suite.sh` and `docs/CONTROLLER.md` (adjacent additions).

Instead, make `reload()` take `now: Instant` as a parameter rather than calling Instant::now() itself, so that after #51 lands it is a one-line change at the call site; the loop's own Instant::now() stays. Run cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test in control/ (all must pass). Prove at least the transient-retry test fails if EBUSY is moved back to the permanent list.
